commits.message: /company read-only company drive and a public folder per Space
commits.body:
The tenant-wide writable /shared is gone. Every run sees /company read-only:
/company/files is the company drive (same storage key as /shared) and
/company/spaces/<key>/ each publishing Space's public/ folder. A Space
shares by writing /space/public — file-tool writes there ask first, the
shell sees it read-only.

- core: company_files_publish / company_files_remove; operations can name
  the capability their approver needs (approverCapability) — agent calls
  always ask, the decision route refuses anyone without it
- core: core.spaces.publish_to_company (NULL follows visibility), surface
  carries companySpaces, GET /api/company/spaces for the UI
- core: file-storage bytes routes check the tenant (they did not); drive
  writes need core.company_files.manage; a person writes a Space's public
  folder only if they can enter it
- ai: /company bound :ro from a host copy refreshed at run start (removes
  unpublished files); /space/public nested :ro; publish approval gate
- ai: sandbox sync propagates deletions to storage
- ui: /company page; Space settings toggle
- docs: mounts, runtime contract, plan

commits.message:
fix(core): give the AI service credential connections and agent provisioning caps

Headless runs (routines, task jobs) call connector actions and provision an
agent's core.agents identity with the AI service token. The locked-down set
held only module.read/write/execute plus the Plan facets, so every routine
calling Gmail got 403 module.connections.read, and core_agents_ensure failed
silently — agents never got a core identity and connection agent grants could
not resolve them ("unknown agent").

AI_SERVICE_CAPABILITIES in plugin-sdk is now the one list the local mint, the
service-token create hint and the docs use. ensure-local replaces a live row
that lacks part of it instead of keeping it.

commits.message:
feat(global): Space-owned connections and a browser per Space

Adopt the Grok-bot model, scoped to Spaces (PLAN-space-owned-connections.md):
a Space is the account. Every agent in it shares the Space's connections, its
computer and its browser logins; each agent gets its own browser window. The
copilot works out of the person's personal Space.

Connections
- module_connections.connections.space_id owns an account; owner_user_id
  becomes connected_by (audit only). sharing, non_owner_max_group,
  all_spaces, connection_agent_grants and connection space mounts are gone
  (fresh start: existing connections are dropped).
- Reach is "the run's Space owns the account". The x-engenty-space-id claim
  is verified (mayUseSpaceInRun): people must be able to enter the Space;
  agents and services only an open Space or their routine's or task's Space.
- Connect (OAuth, API key, local files, browser bridge) requires a Space.
- An ask is decided by the Space's owners or a tenant admin.
- Inbox, calendar sync, files, retrieval and the Slack bridge scope their
  records by the account's Space.
- UI: accounts listed and connected per Space; "Alle Spaces", per-agent
  grants and account mounts removed.

Browser
- One Chromium per Space (engenty-browser-<tenant>-<space>), profile and
  downloads per Space; one window (own tab and seat) per agent.
- Consent per Space in core.space_browser_grants, set by the Space's owners.
- Live view, tickets and routes name the Space and the agent.

chore(global): add prune-tests skill; test outcomes, not functions

Adapt the prune-tests skill to this repo: governed by testing-policy.mdc,
a seam map, the grep-first pattern list, one package per run, the
open/closed commit split. Keep the strict bar (every surviving test
earns its place) and add outcome first: an internal-function test is
redundant when breaking the function already fails an outcome test,
proven by a mutation run without the function's own tests; rewrites
are mutation-checked.

The testing policy no longer calls exported internals fine to test.

commits.message:
fix(ai): a space computer no longer binds the first run's /home for every agent

The space computer is one container per Space, and Docker fixes its binds
when the first run creates it. `/home` was the only per-run bind, so every
later agent's shell saw the first agent's (or person's) home while its file
tools used its own. On a space computer `/home` is now a direct storage
mount reached with file tools only, and the "Your computer" prompt says so.

commits.message:
fix(ai): a space computer no longer binds a staged /data every run shares

The staged /data copy lives in the Space computer's scratch, bound once
for every run in the Space, while each run fills it as its own principal
and flushes it against its own manifest. Materialising never deletes, so
a person's bot could read records staged by another person's run; a
concurrent run could overwrite unflushed edits, or flush another run's
edit under its own approvals.

On a space computer /data is no longer staged or bound; it stays the
direct adapter, reachable with file tools as the run. Per-run sandboxes
keep their staged copy.

commits.message: Space-owned connections and a browser per Space
commits.body:
Adopt the Grok-bot model, scoped to Spaces (PLAN-space-owned-connections.md):
a Space is the account. Every agent in it shares the Space's connections, its
computer and its browser logins; each agent gets its own browser window. The
copilot works out of the person's personal Space.

Connections
- module_connections.connections.space_id owns an account; owner_user_id
  becomes connected_by (audit only). sharing, non_owner_max_group,
  all_spaces, connection_agent_grants and connection space mounts are gone
  (fresh start: existing connections are dropped).
- Reach is "the run's Space owns the account". The x-engenty-space-id claim
  is verified (mayUseSpaceInRun): people must be able to enter the Space;
  agents and services only an open Space or their routine's or task's Space.
- Connect (OAuth, API key, local files, browser bridge) requires a Space.
- An ask is decided by the Space's owners or a tenant admin.
- Inbox, calendar sync, files, retrieval and the Slack bridge scope their
  records by the account's Space.
- UI: accounts listed and connected per Space; "Alle Spaces", per-agent
  grants and account mounts removed.

Browser
- One Chromium per Space (engenty-browser-<tenant>-<space>), profile and
  downloads per Space; one window (own tab and seat) per agent.
- Consent per Space in core.space_browser_grants, set by the Space's owners.
- Live view, tickets and routes name the Space and the agent.

commits.message:
fix(ai): don't nudge a turn the provider failed

Mastra runs isTaskComplete scorers after a step that ended in a provider
error. The empty-reply scorer then forced a second model call after the
error chunk had already ended the AG-UI run: the chat showed 'No response
received', the run settled failed a minute later, and the reply landed in
memory unseen. Skip the nudge when the last message carries Mastra's
error part.

feat(ai): commit model defaults with bindings and apply them on fresh catalogs

activated models (gateway, pricing, availability flags) plus platform role
bindings. The file is bundled at build time, so the Docker image carries it.

  match) and bindings; unknown models/roles are skipped, not errors
- export carries the gateway and the real reasoning price

(pick-one-of-N with confidence, Jev only) and fast_text (short prose
without tools). router, safeguard, planning_coding, research and memory
are gone; migrations move bindings and drop ai.engenty_ai_agents.purpose.

- classifier client reads the classifier binding (TypeSafe key or the
  Vercel TypeSafe route); auto effort, inbox categories, KB verification,
  browser fast loop, tool discovery and guardrails use it and fail open
- fast_text serves titles, inbox digest/summary, starters, hire welcome,
  NL graph query and observational memory; JSON outputs became parsed
  text formats
- supervisors resolve chat, coding agents the high tier; the per-agent
  purpose field is removed

commits.message:
feat(copilot): the river — one private conversation per person, with chapters and an alter ego

The copilot is the person's, not the space's. Its thread is one tenant-wide
private DM per user that follows them everywhere: `/copilot` outside a space,
`/s/<key>/copilot` inside one (a reserved segment; the space's column stays).
It heads the renamed Private section of every space, wears the app-bar blob,
and is never in the Engenties roster. The companion shows the same river.

Gone with it: per-space copilot threads, thread choosers, "new chat", the
copilot app contribution, the `engenty-copilot` URL alias, the legacy chat
routes and their redirects, the dock blob, and every locale key they owned.
Old copilot threads are deleted by the migration — a clean cut.

Each run now carries its own route context (forwardedProps.engenty.
route_context); the server prefers it over the thread's stored one for the
run's space, its language and the place stamped on the user turn
(thread_message.metadata.context) — the river is one thread walked through
many spaces.

Chapters: `ai.thread_compaction` cuts the river into summarised stretches —
one per local day, one per week (cut on read, so an unopened river costs
nothing), or on request ("Compact now"). A rail outside a space, a menu
inside, `?chapter=<id>` opens one above the transcript, and the copilot reads
them with `recall_chapters`. Cadence and retention settings are deferred; the
day boundary is ENGENTY_RIVER_TIME_ZONE (else the process zone).

Alter ego: when the copilot steps into a room for its person it is marked so
(`thread_agent.on_behalf_of_user_id`), its rows say whose it is, and the room
reads "Matthias' Copilot" — the river itself stays private.

Also: `BlobAvatar` gets a real `size` prop; the agent display-name registry is
written in an effect, not during render; the copilot module's memory page
lives under /settings/copilot.

the frame a specialist's desk has — identity block with the compact band
once it scrolls away, the topbar action row (settings, context, browser,
artefacts, ⋮), the settings / runs pane, browser and artefact panes — and

accept a desk line or a DM as well as the river (rooms excluded), the
`recall_chapters` tool follows, and one icon opens them on every desk.

commits.message: the river — one private conversation per person, with chapters and an alter ego
commits.body:
The copilot is the person's, not the space's. Its thread is one tenant-wide
private DM per user that follows them everywhere: `/copilot` outside a space,
`/s/<key>/copilot` inside one (a reserved segment; the space's column stays).
It heads the renamed Private section of every space, wears the app-bar blob,
and is never in the Engenties roster. The companion shows the same river.

Gone with it: per-space copilot threads, thread choosers, "new chat", the
copilot app contribution, the `engenty-copilot` URL alias, the legacy chat
routes and their redirects, the dock blob, and every locale key they owned.
Old copilot threads are deleted by the migration — a clean cut.

Each run now carries its own route context (forwardedProps.engenty.
route_context); the server prefers it over the thread's stored one for the
run's space, its language and the place stamped on the user turn
(thread_message.metadata.context) — the river is one thread walked through
many spaces.

footers.value:
`ai.thread_compaction` cuts the river into summarised stretches —
one per local day, one per week (cut on read, so an unopened river costs
nothing), or on request ("Compact now"). A rail outside a space, a menu
inside, `?chapter=<id>` opens one above the transcript, and the copilot reads
them with `recall_chapters`. Cadence and retention settings are deferred; the
day boundary is ENGENTY_RIVER_TIME_ZONE (else the process zone).

Alter ego: when the copilot steps into a room for its person it is marked so
(`thread_agent.on_behalf_of_user_id`), its rows say whose it is, and the room
reads "Matthias' Copilot" — the river itself stays private.

`BlobAvatar` gets a real `size` prop; the agent display-name registry is
written in an effect, not during render; the copilot module's memory page
lives under /settings/copilot.

commits.message:
fix(ci): stop the open snapshot eating package.json's trailing newline (#21)

The snapshot rewrote package.json through a shell variable to strip the
pro-only plugin slugs. `$(...)` strips every trailing newline and the
`printf '%s'` that fed git hash-object added none back, so the blob ended
at `}`. The mirror's own `Lint (changed files)` then failed biome's format
check on every release — package.json changes each time, so it was always
in the changed set.

Pipe straight into hash-object instead, which keeps the bytes the
transform actually emits (it already ends with a newline).

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ci): give the smoke lane the VITE_ env its browser needs (#20)

* fix(ci): give the smoke lane the VITE_ env its browser needs

The lane has never passed. It wrote SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY to
.env.local but not VITE_SUPABASE_URL/VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, and
apps/ui/vite.config.ts sets envPrefix ["VITE_", "ENV"] — so the SPA's
Supabase client got nothing, threw "Missing Supabase environment", and
/auth/agent-login rendered that error instead of redirecting. Every spec
then timed out in waitForURL on the login page. Both names are
`root: "always"` in packages/cli's env manifest; CI's hand-rolled sed
reimplemented `engenty env init` and dropped them.

Also writes SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET (without it the server lane signs with a
secret the local stack does not know and every tenant query fails), and
fails the step by name when a key comes back empty.

Collateral fixes that kept this invisible: the report upload never
produced a file, because e2e/.report and e2e/.results are dot-directories
and upload-artifact@v4 skips those unless include-hidden-files is set; the
dev server's stdout was discarded in CI; the 60s test timeout was tighter
than a cold Vite transform of the whole module graph; and
reuseExistingServer was unconditionally true, so a stray listener could
become the system under test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(auth): let the dev-login email fall back when ENGENTY_DEV_EMAIL is unset

The session route read the default with envString(), which returns "" for
an unset variable, then chained `?? "agent@engenty.local"`. `??` only
falls through on null/undefined, so the empty string won and the fallback
was unreachable. Supabase then refused with "Cannot create a user without
either an email or phone", and /auth/agent-login rendered that instead of
redirecting — the second wall the smoke lane hit once it had its VITE_ env.

Local checkouts set ENGENTY_DEV_EMAIL via `engenty env init`, so only an
environment that never ran it saw this. Extracted as resolveDevLoginEmail
so the empty-string case is covered by a test; the existing suite always
supplied an address.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(typesafe-client): resolve Jev in one place behind a pooled connection

Every caller — the browser fast loop and the three small classifiers that
follow — turns an environment into a Jev client the same way: resolveJevClient
picks TypeSafe's own API on TYPESAFE_API_KEY, else the Vercel AI Gateway's
TypeSafe-compatible route on AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. isJevConfigured answers the
door question without building a client, so a per-search gate can ask it
cheaply.

The client now fetches through one undici pool with a 60 s keep-alive. Node's
default closes an idle connection after 4 s, and a classifier that runs once
per turn is idle longer than that almost every time: measured 300 ms warm,
400+ ms after a pause (a fresh TLS handshake), 1.4 s in a new process — during
which the event loop is blocked, so a race timer cannot fire. apps/ai spends
one keyed GET at boot to open it, and says so when no key is set: every
symptom of a missing key is otherwise silent.

Also corrects the `score` question type against the live API — criteria is an
ordered array, and an object is a 400 — and moves TYPESAFE_API_KEY into the
AI workspace group, since it is no longer the fast loop's key alone.

commits.message:
feat(ai): Auto effort sizes turns with Jev instead of a language model

The `routing` purpose resolves to a 20B reasoning model that never answered
inside the 250 ms race, so `source: "router"` was effectively dead and the
lexical guess decided every ambiguous turn. Auto now asks Jev one `choice`
question over low|medium|high — the tiers are the option ids, validated
against exactly those, with a 0.5 confidence floor — under an 800 ms budget.
In-process the answer sits at 290–400 ms warm and just over 400 ms after the
pool's idle window; a 400 ms race lost about half the time.

The plan ceiling, the certain heuristics and the fail-open fallback are
unchanged, and only the turns the heuristics could not size pay for this. A
missed budget logs at info with the budget and the measured latency: a
classifier that keeps missing is an operational fact, and debug lines never
print here.

Resolving the run's effort no longer loads the tenant's model bindings — they
were read to pick the router model and nothing else.

commits.message:
feat(inbox): classify message categories with Jev

One call per batch of 20, one `choice` question per message. The criteria are
the tenant's own category rules and the instructions carry the tiebreaker, so
the catalog an admin edits is the catalog the classifier reads. Answers are
validated against exactly the slugs that were offered, and one below the 0.5
confidence floor is left out — the message stays in the default lane like a
miss, and the thread digest refines it later.

This removes about a hundred lines of shape repair: a small model asked for a
JSON index→category map would wrap it, array-ify it or rename the key often
enough to need `coerceCategoryMap`, and a typed question has no shape to get
wrong.

Classifying pending mail also reports failure now. It had no error handler at
all, so the button simply stopped spinning; a missing key gets its own line,
because that is fixed in the environment rather than by retrying.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(wizards): the desk keeps the record's card, not the specialist's JSON

A wizard pressed on a desk left a screen of `{"offer":{…}}` in the
conversation. Three things under that one symptom:

- `run_specialist` opened its step thread with an empty route context, so
  `threadKind` read it as a desk line and the desk opened it as "where you
  left off". The thread now carries the run it belongs to, and the desk feed
  publishes the server's own predicate per engagement (`desk_line`) instead
  of the UI re-deriving it from a flag per kind.
- `POST /workflows/:id/run` ignored the space claim the composer sends (both
  the header and the body), so the run's thread was space-less — and
  everything a run resolves FROM that thread later, the desk it speaks into
  and its memory, had no Space either.
- `runContextFor` dropped `deskAgentId` on a resume or a step back, so every
  card a graph rendered after its first gate went to the run's own log.
  `resolveSpecialistChatThread` may now also find an existing conversation
  without an owner; it still needs one to create the first.

With those, the offers wizard ends by showing what it made: a `show_objects`
node on the created offer, so the conversation holds the record's card. A
mapping cannot fill an element of an array, so the graph primitive takes `ref`
— one canonical ref, as a template — beside the agent tool's `refs`.

Also fixes the dock hanging on "working": the run query stops polling on a
suspended snapshot, and a step that has suspended without a readable gate is
exactly that, so the dock keeps asking until the run parks or settles.

commits.message: Auto effort sizes turns with Jev instead of a language model
commits.body:
The `routing` purpose resolves to a 20B reasoning model that never answered
inside the 250 ms race, so `source: "router"` was effectively dead and the
lexical guess decided every ambiguous turn. Auto now asks Jev one `choice`
question over low|medium|high — the tiers are the option ids, validated
against exactly those, with a 0.5 confidence floor — under an 800 ms budget.
In-process the answer sits at 290–400 ms warm and just over 400 ms after the
pool's idle window; a 400 ms race lost about half the time.

The plan ceiling, the certain heuristics and the fail-open fallback are
unchanged, and only the turns the heuristics could not size pay for this. A
missed budget logs at info with the budget and the measured latency: a
classifier that keeps missing is an operational fact, and debug lines never
print here.

Resolving the run's effort no longer loads the tenant's model bindings — they
were read to pick the router model and nothing else.

commits.message: resolve Jev in one place behind a pooled connection
commits.body:
Every caller — the browser fast loop and the three small classifiers that
follow — turns an environment into a Jev client the same way: resolveJevClient
picks TypeSafe's own API on TYPESAFE_API_KEY, else the Vercel AI Gateway's
TypeSafe-compatible route on AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY. isJevConfigured answers the
door question without building a client, so a per-search gate can ask it
cheaply.

The client now fetches through one undici pool with a 60 s keep-alive. Node's
default closes an idle connection after 4 s, and a classifier that runs once
per turn is idle longer than that almost every time: measured 300 ms warm,
400+ ms after a pause (a fresh TLS handshake), 1.4 s in a new process — during
which the event loop is blocked, so a race timer cannot fire. apps/ai spends
one keyed GET at boot to open it, and says so when no key is set: every
symptom of a missing key is otherwise silent.

Also corrects the `score` question type against the live API — criteria is an
ordered array, and an object is a 400 — and moves TYPESAFE_API_KEY into the
AI workspace group, since it is no longer the fast loop's key alone.

commits.message: stop the open snapshot eating package.json's trailing newline (#21)
commits.body:
The snapshot rewrote package.json through a shell variable to strip the
pro-only plugin slugs. `$(...)` strips every trailing newline and the
`printf '%s'` that fed git hash-object added none back, so the blob ended
at `}`. The mirror's own `Lint (changed files)` then failed biome's format
check on every release — package.json changes each time, so it was always
in the changed set.

Pipe straight into hash-object instead, which keeps the bytes the
transform actually emits (it already ends with a newline).

commits.message:
fix(ci): pre-pull the images production runs, and verify the release after it lands (#19)

The deploy job's forced command pre-pulled `ghcr.io/engenty/engenty-*`
while docker-compose.prebuilt.yaml runs `ghcr.io/engenty/engenty-pro-*`,
so every release downloaded ~20 GB of mirror images nothing would run and
then still pulled the real ones inside the outage window. It also returned
as soon as Coolify had queued the deployment, so "Verify public release"
raced it: v0.2.10 passed against the OLD stack, v0.2.11 and v0.2.12 failed
on releases that were fine.

The installed script was untracked and had drifted from the blue/green
orchestrator its own header claimed to come from. Track it as
deploy/scripts/coolify-queue-deploy.sh, fix the image list (adding
browser), and make it block until Coolify reports the deployment finished,
failing on a failed deployment.

Also renames pro's publish-cli.yml to check-cli-package.yml (it only
dry-runs now) and restores publish-cli.yml as the reviewable source of the
mirror's publisher, guarded to engenty/engenty like publish-images.yml.
Docs and the release skill follow.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(ai): browser_run_fast — classifier-driven browser steps behind a switch

Experimental inner loop for the user browser in the direction of
browser-use/jev-ultrafast: per step, one TypeSafe Jev call picks the
operation and, speculatively, the target for each operation from a
visible-only indexed snapshot (ported from jev-ultrafast, MIT); the
classifier-purpose model writes text only for a typed field. Runs on the
page Mastra's AgentBrowser already holds and goes through the same wrapper
as every browser tool (seat, unattended gate, wake, audit), with one
engenty.browser.action per inner step. Offered only with
ENGENTY_BROWSER_FAST_LOOP on and TYPESAFE_API_KEY present. Model output
never becomes a selector or script; targets are re-checked for freshness
and occlusion before input; a low-confidence step returns uncertain so the
planner LLM takes over.

commits.message:
feat(ai): fast loop picks the best joint step and asks for a page's values once

On busy pages the operation head split between CLICK and TYPE_TEXT (0.3 vs
0.29) while the target heads were sure, and the per-head margin handed the
step back to the LLM. The decision now ranks every (operation, target) pair
by P(operation) × P(target | operation) and gates on the gap between the
best two, so a sure target head breaks an operation tie.

The text helper cost 5–12 s per typed field; it now asks the classifier
model once per page and goal for every typeable field and caches the
answer, so a three-field form is one round trip.

commits.message:
feat(ai): fast loop decides the element first and types from the goal's own words

The classifier's mass no longer splits between "click the field" and "type
into the field": one target head over every element, the element's kind
names the operation, and the operation head is act / scroll / wait / done /
blocked. A close call gets one tiebreak question (this, that, or neither)
before the planner is asked; every non-done note names both candidates and
tells the planner to do that one step and call browser_run_fast again.

Field values come from the classifier picking a span of the goal first; only
a value that has to be rewritten goes to the run's low-tier model, with
minimal reasoning effort, instead of the classifier-tier 20B. Values are
asked for as soon as a page with a field is observed, alongside the
decision. History carries what the field showed after the step.

commits.message:
fix(ai): keep the fast loop from calling a fillable calendar blocked

On Google Flights the classifier kept choosing BLOCKED over clicking the
Done/Search confirmation, handing a half-filled calendar back to the
planner. BLOCKED now means no offered element can advance the goal, and the
next-action rules say to click a visible confirmation (Done, Apply, Search)
rather than re-select a date already set. With this the loop drives the whole
Vienna→Seoul search — cities, both dates, calendar, Search — in one call.

commits.body:

Done/Search confirmation, handing a half-filled calendar back to the
planner. BLOCKED now means no offered element can advance the goal, and the

commits.message: fast loop decides the element first and types from the goal's own words
commits.body:
The classifier's mass no longer splits between "click the field" and "type
into the field": one target head over every element, the element's kind
names the operation, and the operation head is act / scroll / wait / done /
blocked. A close call gets one tiebreak question (this, that, or neither)
before the planner is asked; every non-done note names both candidates and
tells the planner to do that one step and call browser_run_fast again.

Field values come from the classifier picking a span of the goal first; only
a value that has to be rewritten goes to the run's low-tier model, with
minimal reasoning effort, instead of the classifier-tier 20B. Values are
asked for as soon as a page with a field is observed, alongside the
decision. History carries what the field showed after the step.

commits.message: fast loop picks the best joint step and asks for a page's values once
commits.body:
On busy pages the operation head split between CLICK and TYPE_TEXT (0.3 vs
0.29) while the target heads were sure, and the per-head margin handed the
step back to the LLM. The decision now ranks every (operation, target) pair
by P(operation) × P(target | operation) and gates on the gap between the
best two, so a sure target head breaks an operation tie.

The text helper cost 5–12 s per typed field; it now asks the classifier
model once per page and goal for every typeable field and caches the
answer, so a three-field form is one round trip.

commits.body:

finite animation (capped at 1.5 s, spinners ignored), a stale retry settles
before re-observing, and WAIT settles like any input.

commits.message: browser_run_fast — classifier-driven browser steps behind a switch
commits.body:
Experimental inner loop for the user browser in the direction of
browser-use/jev-ultrafast: per step, one TypeSafe Jev call picks the
operation and, speculatively, the target for each operation from a
visible-only indexed snapshot (ported from jev-ultrafast, MIT); the
classifier-purpose model writes text only for a typed field. Runs on the
page Mastra's AgentBrowser already holds and goes through the same wrapper
as every browser tool (seat, unattended gate, wake, audit), with one
engenty.browser.action per inner step. Offered only with
ENGENTY_BROWSER_FAST_LOOP on and TYPESAFE_API_KEY present. Model output
never becomes a selector or script; targets are re-checked for freshness
and occlusion before input; a low-confidence step returns uncertain so the
planner LLM takes over.

CI (verify): the space-storage-scope guard flagged the specialist avatar key
builder in apps/ai/ai/tools/agent-look-preview.ts as unclassified. Agents are
tenant rows (agent_scope personal/shared, no space_id), so classify it as
tenant-level in the allowlist.

db-checks (nightly, never green): every live check shells out through
execSync, i.e. /bin/sh — dash on the runner — and passed psql `-F$'\t'`,
which dash does not understand. The separator arrived as the literal
characters `$\t`, every row parsed as one field, and the grants allowlist
matched nothing. Use '|' in all four scripts (grants, rls, server-lane,
leak-harness) and split on it.

With grants parsing again, the server-lane check surfaced three real
findings, fixed here:
- notifications_select / notification_seen_select (initial schema) called
  auth.uid() directly, which breaks the engenty_server lane at plan time.
  Rewritten on core.current_user_id() and scoped to authenticated; both
  tables already carry srv_tenant_isolation for the server lane.
- core.mcp_client_grants / core.mcp_tasks shipped their server-lane pair
  under bespoke names; renamed to the canonical srv_tenant_isolation.
- public.mcp_oauth_pending_client(text) is deliberately anon-callable (the
  pre-login OAuth consent page); recorded in a new server-lane allowlist
  with the reason.

* fix(db): revoke the public pgmq wrappers from anon and authenticated

On a fresh Supabase database the default privileges for schema public grant
EXECUTE on new functions directly to anon and authenticated; the initial
schema's REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC does not undo a direct grant, so on CI the
browser lane could call the SECURITY DEFINER queue wrappers. The nightly
server-lane check caught it on the first run that got past grants parsing.
Explicit revoke, idempotent, no-op on databases that never had the grant.

commits.message:
feat(routines): let a hired engenty create and edit its own routines

routines_create gains the prompt lane the HTTP route already had (the
server binds and publishes a one-node Workflow — nothing to propose), so
a single-step job never goes through the canvas; workflow_id stays the
lane for more than one step, an approval, or a wait.

Who may call what now comes from the run's identity (caller-scope.ts):
the copilot manages every routine, a coordinator the Space's, a
specialist its own — which it may create too. Whether a person confirms
first is the Space's agent-approval mode (routine-approval.ts): manual
parks on one inline card that publishes the Workflow as that person and
creates the routine on Approve; auto lets the model decide (ask_first
asks anyway) and publishes a draft Workflow as the run; pass-all never
asks. approval_grants always take a card. A run that cannot park refuses
and names the coordinator instead of failing silently. Every creation
lands as a note on the owner's desk and a routine_created inbox row.

workflow_propose no longer parks on its own Publish card for run_by:
routine — routines_create shows the one card — and a specialist can
propose Workflows for itself only.

fix(ai): agent_look takes one object schema, not a top-level union

OpenAI-family providers refuse a function whose parameters are a
top-level anyOf ('schema must be a JSON Schema of type object, got
None'). A hired engenty carries agent_look on every turn, so the first
resume routed to OpenAI took the whole run down — seen live right after
approving a routine card. The per-action requirements now live in a
refinement on a flat object.

commits.message:
feat(cli): engenty setup keeps the local AI service credential alive

core.service_credential is only ever written by a person's bearer, so a
local db reset leaves every checkout's ENGENTY_AI_SERVICE_SECRET naming a
row that no longer exists: apps/ai boots with invalid_client, the
scheduler stays off and routines never fire — silently. setup now ends by
running `engenty service-token ensure-local` (new; local Supabase only,
no bearer): it keeps a secret whose row is live and whose hash matches,
and otherwise mints a platform credential with the locked-down AI set —
the same row shape and sha256 the API writes — and rewrites .env.local.
A live row under the base name is never revoked (another worktree may
hold its secret); the new one takes a dated name.

The CLI's 401 hint now says when the stored session is a Supabase user
token from `auth login --dev`, which core's own routes reject, instead
of sending the person back to that login.

lane for more than one step, an approval, or a wait.

Who may call what now comes from the run's identity (caller-scope.ts):
the copilot manages every routine, a coordinator the Space's, a
specialist its own — which it may create too. Whether a person confirms
first is the Space's agent-approval mode (routine-approval.ts): manual
parks on one inline card that publishes the Workflow as that person and
creates the routine on Approve; auto lets the model decide (ask_first
asks anyway) and publishes a draft Workflow as the run; pass-all never
asks. approval_grants always take a card. A run that cannot park refuses
and names the coordinator instead of failing silently. Every creation
lands as a note on the owner's desk and a routine_created inbox row.

workflow_propose no longer parks on its own Publish card for run_by:
routine — routines_create shows the one card — and a specialist can
propose Workflows for itself only.

commits.message:
feat(chat): state who reads a chat in a header band and sidebar markers

Every conversation now sits in one of three visibility tiers — private
(closed lock), protected (key), open (hash, rooms only) — read the same in
the chat header, the sidebar and the Space's chat list. The desk header's
compact band takes the tier's ground: a private chat flips the theme (the
topbar over it flips along via a new `topbarTone` page-config option),
protected is the ember tint under an ember rule, open the page surface. In
flow, the tier is a chip beside the readers line on the page canvas. The
band is one line: chip, readers sentence, status dot. Rooms wear the same
band. A desk in a personal or private Space is private or protected, not
open — the Space's audience decides.

Design tokens gain a `.tone-flip` scope that turns one region to the other
theme, restating the alias tokens (`--canvas` and friends) and the text
colour so a flipped region resolves its own palette.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(deps): put the Supabase CLI back on the one pin

`chore(deps): minor and patch bumps across the workspace` (a5b9ad6f0)
raised devDependencies.supabase to 2.117.0 but left the pin at 2.113.0 in
packages/cli/src/supabase-cli-version.ts and deploy/Dockerfile.migrate, so
`pnpm check:supabase-pin` failed and took the v0.2.5 "Publish engenty CLI"
run with it.

Restore 2.113.0 rather than raising the other two: the pin file is the
documented source of truth, the migrate image and the deployed lane already
run it, and 2.113.0 → 2.117.0 is 230 upstream commits that promote the
pg-delta rewrite to the default engine and turn shadow-baseline caching on
by default. That upgrade should be its own change, tested against `db up`,
`db migrate` and `db reset` — not a side effect of unbreaking a release.

commits.message:
fix(core): skip closed-module tests on the public snapshot

Three apps/core tests assert behaviour that only exists in engenty-pro, so
they fail in engenty/engenty on every sync: the seat cap comes from the
closed `@engenty/entitlements` package, and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN plus
ENGENTY_REMOTE_CHANNELS_ENABLED are contributed by the closed
`engenty-remote` module's plugin manifest.

Guard them the way entitlements-routes.test.ts already does — `skipIf` on
the real signal, `entitlements` being null and the key being absent from the
settings catalog. Nothing is skipped in engenty-pro, where both are present.

commits.message:
refactor(core): one execution path for module operations

The invoke path existed twice: once throwing InvokeOperationError for
in-process and MCP callers, once building HTTP responses inline. Both
carried the same capability gate, interceptors, policy, approval, space
policy, handler, result policy, audit and events, and the copies had
drifted — different catch order, only one translating a module's typed
errors, and two spellings of the approval body.

invokeOperation is now the only implementation. executeModuleOperation
resolves the principal, calls it, and maps the thrown error through a
single envelope builder, so every status shape lives in one place. The
403 bodies carry a kind because they are otherwise identical.

The two spellings had a consequence: the MCP lane read requestId off the
202 body, which the pipeline spells approvalRequestId, so every approval
round-trip signed its state with an empty id and the client was never
told which request to grant. It reads a typed body now, with a test that
fails on the empty id.

Also lifts requireAuth, contract discovery and the HTTP adapter out of
the 988-line module, and translates a module's typed error from an
interceptor or context filter on every lane, not only HTTP.

commits.message:
feat(ai): run guards, adaptive history budget, real window occupancy

Chat runs on medium-tier models stopped without a word. Three causes, all
outside what the harness could see:

- No time budget: a provider stream that never finished kept the run
  `running` until the process restarted. Every lane now passes Mastra's
  `modelSettings.timeout` (step 3 min, run 20 min; `ENGENTY_AI_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`
  / `ENGENTY_AI_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, 0 disables) and a timeout is a named
  failure (`run_timeout`), not a hang.
- Silent finishes passed as success: `finishReason` "stop" with no text,
  "tool-calls" at the step cap, and a processor tripwire all ended the run
  as completed. They are now named (`empty_reply`, `step_limit`,
  `tripwire`) with a persisted de/en notice, and a text-less stop first gets
  one more step through an `isTaskComplete` scorer whose feedback message
  is kept out of the transcript by the memory adapter. DeepSeek's
  `data_inspection_failed` maps to `content_filtered`.
- Mid-stream provider errors ended the run on the first blip: a
  `StreamErrorRetryProcessor` (2 retries, 1s/2s, `isRetryable` +
  dropped-socket matchers) sits next to the prefill handler.

Two accounting fixes found on the way:

- The recalled-history budget was a fixed 100k for every model. It is now
  derived per agent from the catalog's `context_tokens` minus the measured
  tool block, a reply reserve and the runtime tail
  (`ENGENTY_AI_HISTORY_TOKEN_LIMIT` overrides; 100k when the window is
  unknown).
- `context_prompt_tokens` for delegated (`direct`) runs was the run total:
  the AG-UI bridge attaches usage as one aggregated entry. The lane now
  reads the last step off the Mastra stream, as the chat lane does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): name silent finishes on the headless lane too

Delegated, task and routine runs learned about failures only from the
bridge's RUN_ERROR event, so a timeout arrived flattened and a text-less
stop, a step-cap end or a tripwire were recorded as completed with an
empty result. The headless driver now reads the raw error chunk, the
tripwire chunk and the stream's finish reason through the same helpers
the chat lanes use, and reports them as `streamError`. A run parked on an
approval or stopped by its caller is left alone.

A routine set to "ask" now parks its finished fire instead of reporting and

the overlap guard until the desk's "Reviewed" button (or

line. Agent settings and runs open as a workspace end pane instead of a sheet,
reachable from the agent name in the breadcrumb; the conversation switcher
moved onto the space crumb via a new `routeBreadcrumbAction` page-config slot.
The floating context card now clears that band and steps aside whenever any
end pane is open.

commits.message:
docs(apps): document where Apps run, with the architecture figures

Two pages, split by who they are for. The published one states how an App
is stored, built, released and what its backend can reach. The internal
one keeps the reasoning that would confuse a reader of the first: why a
libSQL server per Space was built and deleted, why source left the jsonb
column, the node:sqlite checkout semantics, and the write-back that is
DAC-checked against the host file's uid — the finding that cost a day.

The drawings are the ones from the design record, ported rather than
redrawn: a `Figure` component carries their class vocabulary (boxes,
text and lines by role) and maps the neutrals onto the site's own tokens,
so one SVG follows light and dark instead of shipping its own palette.
Only the accent and the "this does not work" red stay the figure's own.

Notes for whoever edits these next:

- The pages are `.mdx`, not `.md`. In a `.md` file this pipeline drops
  JSX silently — no error, no escaped markup, the figures simply are not
  in the HTML. These are the repo's first `.mdx` files.
- Markdown links ending in `.md` 404 on the site; fumadocs does not
  rewrite them. These pages link by route. The older pages still use the
  broken form.
- The unbuilt S3 and Drive mounts appear only in the internal page's
  figure, labelled as the proposal they are.

Verified in dev and with a production build, light and dark; the figures
render at 0.88 of full size at desktop width and scroll inside their own
box below 660px.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(projects): phase and project edits land immediately too

Tasks became optimistic in the previous commit, but everything else on the
project-detail page still wrote through `loadProject()` — a full refetch of
the project before anything moved. One screen, two speeds.

Route phase creates, title and date edits, portal visibility, phase deletes
and the project-level writes (settings, briefing, title, tab configuration)
through `beginOptimisticUpdate` on the same `projectKeys.detail(id)` key,
with the document reducers in `lib/project-detail-phase-cache.ts`. A phase's
dates re-derive the project's own start/end the way `fetchProjectWithDateSync`
does on a fetch, so the header moves with the phase.

Deleting a phase settles its tasks first, one write each, and each of those
writes fires a realtime invalidation that can restore the phase mid-sequence;
a realtime DELETE on `project_phases` is not reliably delivered to undo that.
Both deletes therefore re-assert the removal once the server confirms it —
without that, a deleted phase stayed on screen until the next reload.

Drop `useSetContactSettingsMutation` and `useSetContactsRoleMenuConfigMutation`:

commits.message: document where Apps run, with the architecture figures
commits.body:
Two pages, split by who they are for. The published one states how an App
is stored, built, released and what its backend can reach. The internal
one keeps the reasoning that would confuse a reader of the first: why a
libSQL server per Space was built and deleted, why source left the jsonb
column, the node:sqlite checkout semantics, and the write-back that is
DAC-checked against the host file's uid — the finding that cost a day.

The drawings are the ones from the design record, ported rather than
redrawn: a `Figure` component carries their class vocabulary (boxes,
text and lines by role) and maps the neutrals onto the site's own tokens,
so one SVG follows light and dark instead of shipping its own palette.
Only the accent and the "this does not work" red stay the figure's own.

Notes for whoever edits these next:

- The pages are `.mdx`, not `.md`. In a `.md` file this pipeline drops
  JSX silently — no error, no escaped markup, the figures simply are not
  in the HTML. These are the repo's first `.mdx` files.
- Markdown links ending in `.md` 404 on the site; fumadocs does not
  rewrite them. These pages link by route. The older pages still use the
  broken form.
- The unbuilt S3 and Drive mounts appear only in the internal page's
  figure, labelled as the proposal they are.

Verified in dev and with a production build, light and dark; the figures
render at 0.88 of full size at desktop width and scroll inside their own
box below 660px.

commits.message: run guards, adaptive history budget, real window occupancy
commits.body:
Chat runs on medium-tier models stopped without a word. Three causes, all
outside what the harness could see:

- No time budget: a provider stream that never finished kept the run
  `running` until the process restarted. Every lane now passes Mastra's
  `modelSettings.timeout` (step 3 min, run 20 min; `ENGENTY_AI_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS`
  / `ENGENTY_AI_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`, 0 disables) and a timeout is a named
  failure (`run_timeout`), not a hang.
- Silent finishes passed as success: `finishReason` "stop" with no text,
  "tool-calls" at the step cap, and a processor tripwire all ended the run
  as completed. They are now named (`empty_reply`, `step_limit`,
  `tripwire`) with a persisted de/en notice, and a text-less stop first gets
  one more step through an `isTaskComplete` scorer whose feedback message
  is kept out of the transcript by the memory adapter. DeepSeek's
  `data_inspection_failed` maps to `content_filtered`.
- Mid-stream provider errors ended the run on the first blip: a
  `StreamErrorRetryProcessor` (2 retries, 1s/2s, `isRetryable` +
  dropped-socket matchers) sits next to the prefill handler.

Two accounting fixes found on the way:

- The recalled-history budget was a fixed 100k for every model. It is now
  derived per agent from the catalog's `context_tokens` minus the measured
  tool block, a reply reserve and the runtime tail
  (`ENGENTY_AI_HISTORY_TOKEN_LIMIT` overrides; 100k when the window is
  unknown).
- `context_prompt_tokens` for delegated (`direct`) runs was the run total:
  the AG-UI bridge attaches usage as one aggregated entry. The lane now
  reads the last step off the Mastra stream, as the chat lane does.

commits.message: one execution path for module operations
commits.body:
The invoke path existed twice: once throwing InvokeOperationError for
in-process and MCP callers, once building HTTP responses inline. Both
carried the same capability gate, interceptors, policy, approval, space
policy, handler, result policy, audit and events, and the copies had
drifted — different catch order, only one translating a module's typed
errors, and two spellings of the approval body.

invokeOperation is now the only implementation. executeModuleOperation
resolves the principal, calls it, and maps the thrown error through a
single envelope builder, so every status shape lives in one place. The
403 bodies carry a kind because they are otherwise identical.

The two spellings had a consequence: the MCP lane read requestId off the
202 body, which the pipeline spells approvalRequestId, so every approval
round-trip signed its state with an empty id and the client was never
told which request to grant. It reads a typed body now, with a test that
fails on the empty id.

Also lifts requireAuth, contract discovery and the HTTP adapter out of
the 988-line module, and translates a module's typed error from an
interceptor or context filter on every lane, not only HTTP.

commits.message:
refactor(db): consolidate every owner's migrations into one baseline

254 migration files become 28: one per owner, holding the schema as it
stands. Each baseline is a pg_dump of that owner's schemas taken from a
database with the whole history applied, followed by the rows those
migrations seeded — a virgin database holds nothing else, so the data-only
dump is exactly the seed set and the backfills correctly leave nothing
behind.

Proven equal, not assumed: the history and the baselines were applied to two
empty databases and compared. The schema dumps are identical; the seeded rows
are identical as a set. The two differences the diff first showed were real
losses and are fixed here — contacts registers its retrieval source in a
schema it does not own (kept as its own file, at its original version, so it
still runs after that schema exists), and core used to create
srv_tenant_isolation on other modules' tables, which is why every owner is
squashed rather than only the large ones.

A baseline keeps one of its owner's own versions, so a database that ran the
history already has it recorded and never re-runs it. Only invoices moves,
from its earliest version to a later one it already owns, because its schema
references pdf-templates.

Existing databases need their superseded rows cleared from
supabase_migrations.schema_migrations once — the Supabase CLI refuses to push
while the remote knows versions the directory does not. Verified against a
database seeded with all 254 old versions: after the delete, `db push`
reports it up to date and runs no DDL. Documented in architecture.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(cli): run engenty on this machine with `engenty start`

The published package could bootstrap a checkout (`create`) or deploy to a
server (`deploy`), but had no way to just run the thing. `start` is the third
mode: its own Supabase through the pinned CLI, the release's migrations, the
prebuilt containers. `status`, `stop` (`--purge`) and `update` manage it after.

The install lives in `~/.engenty` (`ENGENTY_HOME`), not a folder in the current
directory: the databases are named Docker volumes, so a cwd-relative folder
would be configuration pretending to be the installation, and a second `start`
elsewhere would build a second one. `deploy` keeps writing `./engenty-deploy`,
where the folder really is the operator's deliverable.

The managed stack takes `project_id "engenty"` and a free port band, reusing
the rules `engenty setup` already applies — `supabase-local-stack.mjs` moves
into the package with a re-export left in `scripts/`, as the probes did.
Studio, the log pipeline and the Edge Runtime are off in the generated config:
the first two idle at 190-275 % CPU, and a release ships no
`supabase/functions`, which also makes Edge Runtime the only Supabase container

commits.message:
fix(db): make the consolidated baseline able to build a fresh database

The consolidation dumped with pg_dump, and three of its properties only bite a
database that has never been migrated. Every existing install has the baseline
marked applied and never runs it, which is why nothing caught these until
`engenty start` created a database from scratch.

1. Roles are cluster-global, so pg_dump never emits them. The guarded
   `create role engenty_server` and `grant engenty_server to authenticator`
   from 20260809200000_core_engenty_server_lane.sql were dropped, while 55
   policies in the baseline still grant to that role. A fresh apply died at
   statement 518 with `role "engenty_server" does not exist`.

2. The dump was not schema-only, so it carried 188 `COPY … FROM stdin` data
   sections across 27 files. The migration runner sends statements without a
   stdin stream, so the first one aborted with `No source stream defined`.
   187 were empty and are removed; the one with rows
   (search.source_visibility, four reference rows mapping source types to
   visibility) becomes inserts. No tenant, user, token or audit data was in
   any of them — worth stating, because these files ship to npm and the
   public mirror.

Verified by applying all 22 migrations to a new database.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(cli): make `engenty start` reach a serving app

Found by running it end to end against a new database. Six were in the new
code or its compose overlay, two are older bugs that reach a server too.

In `engenty start`:

- Ship the release's migrations into <home>/supabase/migrations. `supabase
  start` applies them itself when it creates the database, and PostgREST reads
  db-schemas at boot — without them the first start brought up an empty
  database and the API died on `schema "module_…" does not exist`.
- Append sslmode=disable to the local `db push`. It assumes a hosted database
  and negotiates TLS, which local Postgres does not offer.
- Give the containers a container-facing SUPABASE_DB_URL. A host-side
  127.0.0.1 points the migrate container at itself.
- Harvest SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET from `supabase status`. Without it the server
  lane signs with a secret the stack never saw and core refuses to start,
  misreading the rejection as an asymmetric-key project.
- Put the sandbox and spaces trees inside the install. The base compose mounts
  /opt/engenty/... literally, which needs root on a laptop and is not shared
  with Docker Desktop.
- Copy the egress-proxy and browser-proxy directories the compose bind-mounts,
  and make the migrate service a no-op: `start` already applied the migrations
  with the pinned CLI, and the image's own migration set is its release's,
  which collides on a database this package built.

Older, and not specific to `start`:

- The compose never forwarded SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, so the tenant-locked server
  lane could not work on ANY stack that verifies HS256 (local or self-hosted).
- It never forwarded VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY either, so the
  gateway fell back to SUPABASE_URL and served the browser a container-side
  address. Both default to empty, so Cloud deployments are unchanged.
- `engenty deploy` wrote the compose files without the two proxy config
  directories they mount, so a server following the wizard would fail at
  `docker compose up` with "not a directory".

The release images are linux/amd64 only, so the overlay pins the platform and
Docker emulates them; publishing multi-arch is the real fix.

Verified: the app serves on http://localhost:8787, /api/ready and
/initial_setup return 200, and the setup wizard's own gate reports the database
and tenant lane green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): create the Mastra tables on installs without a checkout

apps/ai refuses to start without ai.{mastra_threads, mastra_messages,
mastra_workflow_snapshot}, and nothing outside a checkout created them: the
tables are in no migration, the migrate image only runs `supabase db push`, and
the published ai image built only its server entry, so the init script was not
in it. A brand-new deployment — server or laptop — had apps/ai crash-looping.

The DDL stays out of the migrations on purpose (it belongs to @mastra/pg and
would drift) and off the boot path on purpose (its ~34 idempotent statements
each fire ddl_command_end, which reloads PostgREST's schema cache and 502s
in-flight requests). So it gets what `engenty-migrate` already has: a one-shot
service that runs once per deploy and exits.

- apps/ai builds src/cli/mastra-schema-init.ts as a second entry, so the image
  carries it at apps/ai/dist/cli/mastra-schema-init.js.
- docker-compose.prebuilt.yaml gains `engenty-mastra-init`, which waits for
  engenty-migrate; engenty-edge and engenty-ai now wait for it instead, and
  reach migrate transitively.

Verified against a new database: the service applied 43 tables to ai.* and
apps/ai came up healthy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(core): stop the setup checks passing on a database that is missing tables

`Mastra schema applied — ai.mastra_* present — ok` on a database with zero such
tables. Both probes asked for a HEAD (`head: true`), and PostgREST answers a
HEAD with no body, so supabase-js had nothing to build an error from: a 404 for
a table that does not exist arrived as `error: null`. They now issue a real GET
with `limit(0)`, which is as cheap and carries the error body.

The test's fake client is why this survived its own suite — it made `select()`
terminal, so the arguments the real builder cares about were never exercised.
It now has the builder's shape.

Also repoints the three SQL guards at the consolidated baseline. They pinned
migrations the consolidation replaced, so they had been failing since
217d43e92: `latestBaselineMigration()` found no file and threw. The invariants
all survive in the dump, in its spelling — `CREATE FUNCTION` without `or
replace`, spelled-out types, `'open'::text` casts, `( select f() as f)` for a
scalar subquery, and named parameters in the function grants.

One assertion is dropped rather than restated: the one-time deletion of
pre-existing member rows on personal spaces was a migration step, and a dump of
the resulting schema legitimately has no trace of it. The trigger that forbids
creating such a row is still pinned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message: stop the setup checks passing on a database that is missing tables
commits.body:
`Mastra schema applied — ai.mastra_* present — ok` on a database with zero such
tables. Both probes asked for a HEAD (`head: true`), and PostgREST answers a
HEAD with no body, so supabase-js had nothing to build an error from: a 404 for
a table that does not exist arrived as `error: null`. They now issue a real GET
with `limit(0)`, which is as cheap and carries the error body.

The test's fake client is why this survived its own suite — it made `select()`
terminal, so the arguments the real builder cares about were never exercised.
It now has the builder's shape.

Also repoints the three SQL guards at the consolidated baseline. They pinned
migrations the consolidation replaced, so they had been failing since
217d43e92: `latestBaselineMigration()` found no file and threw. The invariants
all survive in the dump, in its spelling — `CREATE FUNCTION` without `or
replace`, spelled-out types, `'open'::text` casts, `( select f() as f)` for a
scalar subquery, and named parameters in the function grants.

One assertion is dropped rather than restated: the one-time deletion of
pre-existing member rows on personal spaces was a migration step, and a dump of
the resulting schema legitimately has no trace of it. The trigger that forbids
creating such a row is still pinned.

commits.message: create the Mastra tables on installs without a checkout
commits.body:
apps/ai refuses to start without ai.{mastra_threads, mastra_messages,
mastra_workflow_snapshot}, and nothing outside a checkout created them: the
tables are in no migration, the migrate image only runs `supabase db push`, and
the published ai image built only its server entry, so the init script was not
in it. A brand-new deployment — server or laptop — had apps/ai crash-looping.

The DDL stays out of the migrations on purpose (it belongs to @mastra/pg and
would drift) and off the boot path on purpose (its ~34 idempotent statements
each fire ddl_command_end, which reloads PostgREST's schema cache and 502s
in-flight requests). So it gets what `engenty-migrate` already has: a one-shot
service that runs once per deploy and exits.

- apps/ai builds src/cli/mastra-schema-init.ts as a second entry, so the image
  carries it at apps/ai/dist/cli/mastra-schema-init.js.
- docker-compose.prebuilt.yaml gains `engenty-mastra-init`, which waits for
  engenty-migrate; engenty-edge and engenty-ai now wait for it instead, and
  reach migrate transitively.

Verified against a new database: the service applied 43 tables to ai.* and
apps/ai came up healthy.

commits.message: make `engenty start` reach a serving app
commits.body:
Found by running it end to end against a new database. Six were in the new
code or its compose overlay, two are older bugs that reach a server too.

In `engenty start`:

- Ship the release's migrations into <home>/supabase/migrations. `supabase
  start` applies them itself when it creates the database, and PostgREST reads
  db-schemas at boot — without them the first start brought up an empty
  database and the API died on `schema "module_…" does not exist`.
- Append sslmode=disable to the local `db push`. It assumes a hosted database
  and negotiates TLS, which local Postgres does not offer.
- Give the containers a container-facing SUPABASE_DB_URL. A host-side
  127.0.0.1 points the migrate container at itself.
- Harvest SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET from `supabase status`. Without it the server
  lane signs with a secret the stack never saw and core refuses to start,
  misreading the rejection as an asymmetric-key project.
- Put the sandbox and spaces trees inside the install. The base compose mounts
  /opt/engenty/... literally, which needs root on a laptop and is not shared
  with Docker Desktop.
- Copy the egress-proxy and browser-proxy directories the compose bind-mounts,
  and make the migrate service a no-op: `start` already applied the migrations
  with the pinned CLI, and the image's own migration set is its release's,
  which collides on a database this package built.

Older, and not specific to `start`:

- The compose never forwarded SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, so the tenant-locked server
  lane could not work on ANY stack that verifies HS256 (local or self-hosted).
- It never forwarded VITE_SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY either, so the
  gateway fell back to SUPABASE_URL and served the browser a container-side
  address. Both default to empty, so Cloud deployments are unchanged.
- `engenty deploy` wrote the compose files without the two proxy config
  directories they mount, so a server following the wizard would fail at
  `docker compose up` with "not a directory".

The release images are linux/amd64 only, so the overlay pins the platform and
Docker emulates them; publishing multi-arch is the real fix.

footers.value:
the app serves on http://localhost:8787, /api/ready and
/initial_setup return 200, and the setup wizard's own gate reports the database
and tenant lane green.

commits.message: make the consolidated baseline able to build a fresh database
commits.body:
The consolidation dumped with pg_dump, and three of its properties only bite a
database that has never been migrated. Every existing install has the baseline
marked applied and never runs it, which is why nothing caught these until
`engenty start` created a database from scratch.

1. Roles are cluster-global, so pg_dump never emits them. The guarded
   `create role engenty_server` and `grant engenty_server to authenticator`
   from 20260809200000_core_engenty_server_lane.sql were dropped, while 55
   policies in the baseline still grant to that role. A fresh apply died at
   statement 518 with `role "engenty_server" does not exist`.

2. The dump was not schema-only, so it carried 188 `COPY … FROM stdin` data
   sections across 27 files. The migration runner sends statements without a
   stdin stream, so the first one aborted with `No source stream defined`.
   187 were empty and are removed; the one with rows
   (search.source_visibility, four reference rows mapping source types to
   visibility) becomes inserts. No tenant, user, token or audit data was in
   any of them — worth stating, because these files ship to npm and the
   public mirror.

Verified by applying all 22 migrations to a new database.

commits.message: run engenty on this machine with `engenty start`
commits.body:
The published package could bootstrap a checkout (`create`) or deploy to a
server (`deploy`), but had no way to just run the thing. `start` is the third
mode: its own Supabase through the pinned CLI, the release's migrations, the
prebuilt containers. `status`, `stop` (`--purge`) and `update` manage it after.

The install lives in `~/.engenty` (`ENGENTY_HOME`), not a folder in the current
directory: the databases are named Docker volumes, so a cwd-relative folder
would be configuration pretending to be the installation, and a second `start`
elsewhere would build a second one. `deploy` keeps writing `./engenty-deploy`,
where the folder really is the operator's deliverable.

The managed stack takes `project_id "engenty"` and a free port band, reusing
the rules `engenty setup` already applies — `supabase-local-stack.mjs` moves
into the package with a re-export left in `scripts/`, as the probes did.
Studio, the log pipeline and the Edge Runtime are off in the generated config:
the first two idle at 190-275 % CPU, and a release ships no
`supabase/functions`, which also makes Edge Runtime the only Supabase container
without a restart policy.

`docker-compose.local.yaml` publishes the edge port and adds `host-gateway`,
because Supabase runs in the Supabase CLI's own compose project. The base
compose stays a server file — its comment explains why it publishes no port.

Also adds `engenty env set <key> <value>`, the non-interactive sibling of
`env edit`, and a `home` scope that answers under the deploy contract. Outside
a checkout the manifest holds only core variables, since module
`engenty.plugin.json` files are not in the package, so an unknown key there is
written with a note rather than refused.

the first two idle at 190-275 % CPU, and a release ships no

without a restart policy.

because Supabase runs in the Supabase CLI's own compose project. The base
compose stays a server file — its comment explains why it publishes no port.

`env edit`, and a `home` scope that answers under the deploy contract. Outside
a checkout the manifest holds only core variables, since module

written with a note rather than refused.

commits.message: consolidate every owner's migrations into one baseline
commits.body:
254 migration files become 28: one per owner, holding the schema as it
stands. Each baseline is a pg_dump of that owner's schemas taken from a
database with the whole history applied, followed by the rows those
migrations seeded — a virgin database holds nothing else, so the data-only
dump is exactly the seed set and the backfills correctly leave nothing
behind.

Proven equal, not assumed: the history and the baselines were applied to two
empty databases and compared. The schema dumps are identical; the seeded rows
are identical as a set. The two differences the diff first showed were real
losses and are fixed here — contacts registers its retrieval source in a
schema it does not own (kept as its own file, at its original version, so it
still runs after that schema exists), and core used to create
srv_tenant_isolation on other modules' tables, which is why every owner is
squashed rather than only the large ones.

A baseline keeps one of its owner's own versions, so a database that ran the
history already has it recorded and never re-runs it. Only invoices moves,
from its earliest version to a later one it already owns, because its schema
references pdf-templates.

Existing databases need their superseded rows cleared from
supabase_migrations.schema_migrations once — the Supabase CLI refuses to push
while the remote knows versions the directory does not. Verified against a
database seeded with all 254 old versions: after the delete, `db push`
reports it up to date and runs no DDL. Documented in architecture.md.

commits.message:
fix(setup): never install against another checkout's database; ask how the app is opened

The first public test install (2026-09-13) wrote its administrator, team
and space into a different checkout's database and ended with a copilot
that could not reach apps/ai. Five defects, all in the setup path:

- .env.example shipped SUPABASE_URL / VITE_SUPABASE_URL / SUPABASE_DB_URL as
  values, so env init saw them as set and never read `supabase status`;
  a stack on another port band kept the default band. The three carry no
  default now, env init always harvests them, refuses a stack whose port is
  not this checkout's supabase/config.toml, and rewrites the block on a
  rerun when the file names another stack's port. doctor has the same row.
- "Optional: run portless:setup?" became "How will you open engenty?":
  localhost (default) or Portless, Portless only when the CLI is installed.
  `engenty dev` warns when the dev-URL block and the start mode disagree.
- env init ran after migrations, so the Mastra schema step never saw
  SUPABASE_DB_URL on a first run and skipped. env init runs first now.
- "Environment ready" printed under "1 need attention"; the verdict and
  the summary count the same rows, a skipped key names what stays off, and
  `engenty setup` exits 1 on remaining gaps unless --allow-gaps.
- The first-space step creates the space when the tenant has no default
  instead of failing with nothing to skip to.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(cli): move the command implementations to packages/cli and publish them as the `engenty` npm package

`npx engenty …` is a door, not a second CLI: inside a checkout it hands the
command line to that checkout's `pnpm engenty …`; anywhere else it offers
`create` (prerequisites → clone at this release → pnpm install → the
checkout's `engenty setup`), `deploy` (the wizard, working in
./engenty-deploy/ with the compose templates so a server needs no clone),
`deploy migrate` (the release's baked migrations via SUPABASE_DB_URL and a
pinned Supabase CLI fetched through npx) and `doctor` (host prerequisites,
`--remote`).

- packages/cli (@engenty/cli): setup, generate, dev, doctor, db, reset,
  env, deploy, create, plugin-manifest ops; apps/core keeps auth, tools,
  skills, service-token, plugin-create and registers the rest from the
  package (error hint injected via setCliErrorHint). mandatory-plugins now
  lives in @engenty/environment.
- the deploy wizard moves to packages/cli/wizard (deploy/scripts shim), the
  Supabase probes to packages/cli/lib (scripts/lib shim); both read the
  release manifest outside a checkout.
- scripts/publish-cli.mjs stages the package as `engenty` at the release
  version with only the open schemas/migrations and public image names;
  publish-cli.yml runs it on v* tags, dry-run until PUBLISH_CLI_ENABLED and
  NPM_TOKEN exist.
- one Supabase CLI pin (packages/cli/src/supabase-cli-version.ts), checked
  against the root devDependency and Dockerfile.migrate by check:supabase-pin.
- README, www quick start, setup docs, DEPLOY.md, releases doc, AGENTS.md and
  the release skill describe the two modes.

commits.message:
fix(cli): Mastra init sees the env file setup just wrote; browser-settable keys never fail setup; rebuild after pull

Three findings from the second fresh install:

- `engenty setup` ran env init and then the Mastra schema step in the same
  process, whose environment was loaded at start — the child got no
  SUPABASE_DB_URL and skipped, silently leaving apps/ai without its tables.
  The init child now reads the connection string from the env files at that
  moment, and the file wins over a value the process holds from boot.
- The env wizard exited 1 for the empty AI provider key, so setup "failed"
  on the exact key the first-run wizard asks for. Platform-configurable
  gaps are reported as "set in the browser" and do not fail the run.
- A `dist` that exists was taken as current: after `git pull` the CLI and
  core's dependencies were stale until a manual build. The wrapper stamps
  the commit it last built at and refreshes through turbo when it changes.

Also: doctor no longer reports the www port on a tree that ships no www.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(publish): prune pnpm-lock.yaml to the open tree in the snapshot

The mirror's lockfile still carried an importer for every closed workspace
package and the packages only they pulled in, so the first `pnpm install`
in any clone rewrote it and `--frozen-lockfile` could never pass there.
The snapshot now runs `pnpm install --lockfile-only` on the materialised
tree, hashes the result into the index, and refuses to publish if a closed
importer survives.

commits.message: write SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET from supabase status; gate row for the tenant lane
commits.body:
The env manifest had no SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, so engenty env init never
wrote one and the tenant-locked server lane in core and apps/ai signed
its engenty_server tokens with the random ENGENTY_SECURITY_JWT_SECRET —
PostgREST rejected every tenant-lane query with "No suitable key or
wrong key type" (the notifications delivery tick logged it every 30s).

Core only logs a failed lane preflight outside production, so the
wizard's readiness gate now runs the same probe and fails with the
env-init fix instead of letting the install proceed into that state.

  arrived so the picker fills without a restart

  counts every key, plugin declares OPPER_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

commits.message: prune pnpm-lock.yaml to the open tree in the snapshot
commits.body:
The mirror's lockfile still carried an importer for every closed workspace
package and the packages only they pulled in, so the first `pnpm install`
in any clone rewrote it and `--frozen-lockfile` could never pass there.
The snapshot now runs `pnpm install --lockfile-only` on the materialised
tree, hashes the result into the index, and refuses to publish if a closed
importer survives.
commits.raw_message:
fix(publish): prune pnpm-lock.yaml to the open tree in the snapshot

The mirror's lockfile still carried an importer for every closed workspace
package and the packages only they pulled in, so the first `pnpm install`
in any clone rewrote it and `--frozen-lockfile` could never pass there.
The snapshot now runs `pnpm install --lockfile-only` on the materialised
tree, hashes the result into the index, and refuses to publish if a closed
importer survives.

commits.message: Mastra init sees the env file setup just wrote; browser-settable keys never fail setup; rebuild after pull
commits.body:
Three findings from the second fresh install:

- `engenty setup` ran env init and then the Mastra schema step in the same
  process, whose environment was loaded at start — the child got no
  SUPABASE_DB_URL and skipped, silently leaving apps/ai without its tables.
  The init child now reads the connection string from the env files at that
  moment, and the file wins over a value the process holds from boot.
- The env wizard exited 1 for the empty AI provider key, so setup "failed"
  on the exact key the first-run wizard asks for. Platform-configurable
  gaps are reported as "set in the browser" and do not fail the run.
- A `dist` that exists was taken as current: after `git pull` the CLI and
  core's dependencies were stale until a manual build. The wrapper stamps
  the commit it last built at and refreshes through turbo when it changes.

footers.value: doctor no longer reports the www port on a tree that ships no www.

commits.message: move the command implementations to packages/cli and publish them as the `engenty` npm package
commits.body:
`npx engenty …` is a door, not a second CLI: inside a checkout it hands the
command line to that checkout's `pnpm engenty …`; anywhere else it offers
`create` (prerequisites → clone at this release → pnpm install → the
checkout's `engenty setup`), `deploy` (the wizard, working in
./engenty-deploy/ with the compose templates so a server needs no clone),
`deploy migrate` (the release's baked migrations via SUPABASE_DB_URL and a
pinned Supabase CLI fetched through npx) and `doctor` (host prerequisites,
`--remote`).

- packages/cli (@engenty/cli): setup, generate, dev, doctor, db, reset,
  env, deploy, create, plugin-manifest ops; apps/core keeps auth, tools,
  skills, service-token, plugin-create and registers the rest from the
  package (error hint injected via setCliErrorHint). mandatory-plugins now
  lives in @engenty/environment.
- the deploy wizard moves to packages/cli/wizard (deploy/scripts shim), the
  Supabase probes to packages/cli/lib (scripts/lib shim); both read the
  release manifest outside a checkout.
- scripts/publish-cli.mjs stages the package as `engenty` at the release
  version with only the open schemas/migrations and public image names;
  publish-cli.yml runs it on v* tags, dry-run until PUBLISH_CLI_ENABLED and
  NPM_TOKEN exist.
- one Supabase CLI pin (packages/cli/src/supabase-cli-version.ts), checked
  against the root devDependency and Dockerfile.migrate by check:supabase-pin.
- README, www quick start, setup docs, DEPLOY.md, releases doc, AGENTS.md and
  the release skill describe the two modes.

commits.message: first-run wizard with a readiness gate, AI provider, personal space and Ready screen
commits.body:
The browser wizard now starts with a gate that shows what `engenty setup`
should have left behind — core's checks (database, Mastra schema, apps/ai
reachable, baseline modules, provider key) plus the browser's own probe of
the AI URL the UI was built with — and blocks with the terminal command
until every red row is green. Then: administrator, team, AI provider
(Vercel AI Gateway or OpenRouter, with "Test key" against the gateway's
auth endpoint; stored as a platform setting), first space (create or
rename), the optional personal-space step, and a Ready screen that is the
only place the shared client signs in.

A platform setting saved through the API is live at once: core applies it
to its own environment (restoring the boot value when a row is cleared) and
calls apps/ai's new `POST /ai/internal/settings/reload` with a service
token it signs itself. Observability sinks stay boot-only and are named as
such in the reload answer.
