commits.message: stop a snapshot resume re-persisting the user turn it is resuming
commits.body:
Answering a decision card wrote the user's original question to the thread a
SECOND time, so the model re-read it on every later turn and the chat showed it
twice on reload.

Mastra delivers user turns as SIGNAL messages, and the id of the signal MESSAGE
is not stable across runs. The start run persisted the row under one id; the
snapshot resume — which rebuilds the turn from Mastra's own workflow state rather
than from our rows — re-saved the same turn under another. Keyed only on
`message.id`, the second save matched nothing and inserted a duplicate.

The turn's durable identity is the signal id, which survives both paths and was
already being persisted in row metadata; both copies in the thread that surfaced
this carry the same one. A user row now matches on it when the message id does
not. Role-gated, because folding a user turn onto an assistant row would
overwrite the model's answer with the question.

Found by reading the AG-UI inspector's timeline top-down, which is what the
preceding ordering fix was about.

commits.message: open the context meter's prompt number into a size breakdown
commits.body:
Developer mode turns the composer's "Prompt 29.9k" into a link; it opens a modal
splitting the prompt into system instructions, recalled history and tool
definitions, with tools listed heaviest first.

RECONSTRUCTED on request, not captured per run. Storing each run's assembled
prompt would duplicate the whole conversation every turn (~120KB for a 30k-token
prompt) for a read almost nobody performs, and would put a second copy of that
content under a different retention rule than the thread it came from. The cost
is that this describes the NEXT run rather than the last one, so it does not
match the meter's `prompt_tokens` — which is stated in the panel rather than
smoothed over, and is also what makes it useful: it moves as you prune.

`GET /ai/v1/threads/:id/prompt-preview` assembles the agent through the same
`resolveAgentForSessionMemory` a run uses, but deliberately WITHOUT a run id — a
run id is what makes that function write an `ai.agent_run` row and provision
workspaces and sandboxes, which a GET that only reads sizes has no business
causing. What that costs (workspace tools) goes out as a caveat rather than
quietly shrinking the total. Dev-only, 404 in production, same switch as the
AG-UI debug firehose.

Verified against the live dev thread, which caught the one bug that mattered:
tools arriving from `getToolsForExecution` are AI SDK CoreTools whose
`parameters` is the SDK's `Schema` wrapper, not a Zod type, so a Zod-only
conversion measured all 46 tools at zero and reported the prompt's HEAVIEST
section as weightless — 12k chars instead of 36.6k. Tool schemas turn out to be
59% of that thread's prompt, which is the whole answer the panel exists to give.
Unreadable schemas now report `schema_source: "none"` and name themselves in the

Developer mode turns the composer's "Prompt 29.9k" into a link; it opens a modal
splitting the prompt into system instructions, recalled history and tool

causing. What that costs (workspace tools) goes out as a caveat rather than
quietly shrinking the total. Dev-only, 404 in production, same switch as the

commits.message: route the decision card by tool name, not by tool output
commits.body:
The chooser was registered with `match: (ctx) => matchesDecisionArtifactOutput(
ctx.output)` — it decided whether to render from the tool call's OUTPUT. A
natively suspended `requestDecision` has no output, so the match failed and the
call fell through to the generic card: a spinning "Decision needed" row with no
way to answer it. The choices were on the wire the whole time; nothing was
listening, because the component that reads the open interrupt was never the one
being rendered.

Matching on tool name as well hands those calls to the card that knows how to
hydrate from the open interrupt. The output arm stays: tool-approval cards still
arrive as an artifact result under `engenty_tool_execute`.

Routing by name means the card now also sees answered and dangling decision
calls, which brings three consequences with it:

- No artifact resolves for those, and returning null erased the tool call from
  the turn entirely. They fall back to the normal transcript row.
- Every unanswered decision row would otherwise render whichever chooser is
  currently open — the same question several times, only one of which can be
  answered. The open interrupt now only hydrates the call it names.
- An open interrupt on this call counts as "waiting". `pendingInterruptToolCall-
  Ids` is populated from RUN_FINISHED, so after a reload it is empty and an
  unanswered card reported itself as "Decision submitted".

commits.message: stop the native decision suspend from losing and duplicating its turn
commits.body:
`requestDecision` suspends the run instead of returning its artifact as a tool
result, which quietly invalidated two assumptions the surrounding code still
encoded.

"The artifact arrives as a tool RESULT" — `emitArtifactInterrupt` was the only
one of the three interrupt emitters not putting the card on the CUSTOM
`engenty.open_interrupt` side channel. It never needed to: the client could read
the artifact off the result. With no result and no event, the RUN_FINISHED
outcome (schema-stripped to an id and a title, no choices) was all that reached
the browser.

"An interrupted turn leaves NOTHING behind" — memory flushed only at
end-of-generation back when a decision ABORTED the run, so the executor wrote the
transcript itself as a safety net. A suspend keeps the turn inside Mastra, which
flushes on park; the safety net became a second copy of the same tool call, once
as `tool-invocation` and once as `dynamic-tool`. Both lanes now stand down on
parked paths. `native-suspend-memory-flush.test.ts` pins that against the real
runtime rather than assuming it.

Two more that fell out of the above:

- `resolveToolCallResultInHistory` only ever patched memory's shape and stopped
  at the first row, so an answered decision left its duplicate spinning. It now
  resolves both shapes and every row carrying the call, which also repairs
  threads that already hold doubles.
- The snapshot lane handed its converter over by RETURN VALUE, so a continuation
  that died mid-stream threw past the handover and the post-run pass silently did
  nothing — dropping the half-answer, the sub-agent log and the token count for
  exactly the failure it exists to salvage. It is handed over the moment it
  exists now.

commits.message: give the resume lanes the executor's post-run pass
commits.body:
Neither resume lane ran the teardown the START executor has always run, so
everything a resumed turn produced after the gate was invisible: the
transcript, the sub-agent Log, and the tokens.

The case that needs it most is the one Mastra memory can never cover. A
continuation ending on a SECOND suspend never reaches end-of-generation, so
memory flushes nothing at all — the whole continuation was lost, and the
next turn read an empty transcript and re-asked the question the user had
already answered. Multi-hop approvals (approve -> tool -> approve again)
are the common shape, not an exotic one. The pass therefore lives in
`finally`, where every exit path reaches it.

Metering was the same story from the other end: a gated turn does its cheap
half before the approval and its expensive half after, and only the first
half was ever billed. A failed resume also stored `error_message = NULL`,
which is exactly the field you go looking for afterwards.

`DurableAgUiConverter` gained the state this needs — transcript parts, a
`lastUsage` from the `finish` chunk, and resolved/suspended tracking — so
the snapshot lane can also answer a tool the model invents mid-continuation
instead of leaving its card spinning forever. A tool that SUSPENDED is
tracked apart from one that dangles: settling it would resolve the very
interrupt the run just raised.

`usageFromSession`/`recordSessionUsage` move to run-usage.ts rather than
being copied, so both executors meter through one implementation.

commits.message: make the snapshot resume exclusive and rebuild its agent context
commits.body:
Two more members of the "a re-assembled agent has none of it" family, both
of which only misbehave AFTER a restart — which is precisely when nobody is
watching.

Mutual exclusion. `takeParkedSessionRun` claims the in-flight marker for
the parked lane, but on the snapshot lane it returns nothing, so that lane
had no mutual exclusion at all: two answers for one run executed
concurrently, each resolving AND destroying the single session-scoped
sandbox (the second continuation then hit SandboxNotReadyError, plus a
syncOut race over one staging dir). Both were also invisible to the
thread-load reconciler, which reads that same marker as proof an interrupt
is still live, so a concurrent load could clear an interrupt mid-resume.
`claimResumeInFlight` is a check-and-set the snapshot lane owns and
releases; the `finally` now releases only a claim this call actually made.

Agent context. The re-assembled agent was given no instruction overrides,
no per-run runtime instructions, and no model config — the parked lane
inherits all three from its live Session. The visible symptom is language:
`route_context` carries the user's UI language, so a German user's
post-restart continuation came back in English. Persona and skill overrides
vanished the same way, and the continuation could answer on a different
model than the first half of its own turn. Instructions ride
`instructionExtras.appendBodies`, which is where the controller's per-run
instructions land on the start lane; resolution is best-effort, since
degraded instructions beat a stranded interrupt.

Still missing on this lane and deliberately left out of scope: delegation
tools, which need child-workspace plumbing the resume input does not carry.

commits.message: scope the portal client lookup to the project's tenant
commits.body:
The portal resolved a project's client name by reading module_contacts by
id alone. The adapter from getDatabaseAdapter() is service-role and
bypasses RLS, and projects.client_id is plain text with no foreign key, so
nothing confined that read to the project's own tenant — and the portal
visitor is anonymous, so the result renders on a public page.

The read also named module_contacts.entities, which no longer exists: the
contacts migration replaced entities/people/contact_organisation with
module_contacts.contacts. So it has been erroring on every portal load and
falling through to the stored client_name. Point it at contacts and route
it through foreignSelect, which takes the tenant scope as a required
argument. Scope comes from the project row itself, as getPublicGeneralTasks
and createRequestTask already do here; single() becomes maybeSingle() so a
client_id with no in-tenant match is an ordinary miss rather than an error.

Where a project has a real client_id the portal now shows the contact's
display_name instead of the stored client_name string. That is what this
code always intended, but it is visible if the two have drifted apart.

Drops the matching BASELINE entry from the guardrail; the other two sites
it named were already fixed in 72454c190.

commits.message: add free-text notes to a saved report
commits.body:
A saved report could carry a title and nothing else, so the reasoning
behind a report — what period it covers, what was excluded, who asked
for it — lived outside the tool. `notes` is edited inline under the
report heading and persists on the saved_reports row.

Nullable with no default: an absent note and an empty note mean the same
thing, so existing reports stay valid without a backfill.

Notes are deliberately NOT carried in the URL. Every other part of the
builder state round-trips through search params so a report is
shareable as a link, but prose would bloat every navigation, and the
saved report is the only meaningful source for it — an unsaved draft
simply starts empty. reportStateFromSavedFilters now takes the notes
alongside the title for the same reason.

Also persists the three *_contains predicates
(client_name_contains, project_name_contains, notes_contains) on
SavedTimeReportFilters. They were added to the filter row UI but not to
the saved shape, so reopening a saved report silently dropped them.

Printing renders the notes under the heading and hides the inline edit
affordance.

commits.message: give tenantless join tables a real tenant boundary
commits.body:
Module DAL runs on a service-role client that bypasses RLS, so every
tenant boundary is application-level. Five join tables had none of their
own: their RLS policies reached through a parent to find the tenant, and
with RLS bypassed that join was the only thing separating tenants. Any
reader that skipped it turned a foreign id into an authoritative answer
— which is how the secrets reveal path came to grant cross-tenant access
via project_team.

Each table now carries tenant_id/scope_id backed by a composite foreign
key against (id, tenant_id, scope_id) on its parent, so a row that
disagrees with its own parent is unrepresentable and a parent changing
scope drags its children along:

  module_projects.project_team              20260809120000
  module_tasks.task_collaborators           20260809140000
  module_contacts.contact_roles             20260809141000
  module_kb.article_tags / faq_tags         20260809142000
  module_kb.kb_source_item_{sections,media,links}
                                            20260809143000

task_collaborators was the worst placed: three modules read it and two
keyed on user_id alone, which is global, so those reads returned task
ids from every tenant that user touched.

The kb tag joins needed a different recipe. They have TWO tenant-scoped
parents, so a column alone would not stop an article being tagged with
another tenant's tag — both composite FKs point at the same
(tenant_id, scope_id) pair, forcing owner and tag into one tenant. Those
two FKs must be DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED: two ON UPDATE CASCADE
constraints sharing a column pair otherwise deadlock, because moving an
article's scope cascades the join row onto a tag that has not moved yet.
Verified in psql across insert, cross-tenant insert, scope move and
cascade delete.

Two unbounded cross-tenant scans closed along the way, both of the shape
that produced the secrets leak — ids fetched across all tenants and only
narrowed by a later filter:
  - contacts listContactIdsByRole, .eq("role") with nothing else
  - knowledge-base article search by tag_id

Guard changes (scripts/check-foreign-schema-scope.mjs):
  - UNSCOPED_TABLES is now deliberately empty. task_collaborators was
    its last entry and did not survive scrutiny; wanting to add one is
    the signal a table needs a boundary instead.
  - Accepts an insert/upsert that sets tenant_id and scope_id in the
    payload — a write carries its tenant there, not in a filter.
  - BASELINE 5 -> 3; the project-tasks-bridge entries are fixed.

Also drops two tables the audit found dead — no readers, no rows, no FK
children, no views or functions: module_projects.portal_rate_limits
(20260809144000) and module_secrets.service_secrets (20260809145000).

All five tenant migrations are re-runnable: the child composite FK is
dropped first, since it depends on the parent unique index the migration
recreates.

commits.message: fail loudly when a snapshot resume cannot finish
commits.body:
Two ways the crash-recovery lane reported SUCCESS for a run that had in
fact failed or was still waiting. Both matter more than the missing
answer, because the success path CLEARS the open interrupt — and that
metadata key is the only pointer back to the suspended run, so once it is
gone no reconciler, reload, or retry can reach the turn again.

`DurableAgUiConverter` has no case for Mastra's in-band `error` chunk, and
nothing inspected `finishReason` either (`readMastraStreamFailure` exists
for exactly that and had no callers). A gateway failure mid-continuation
therefore reached neither the client nor the run row: the thread flipped
to completed and the interrupt was deleted. Both signals are now read and
raised. The parked lane gets this from its session's `error` event.

The second is narrower and newer: when a re-suspend cannot be rendered as
an interrupt — a frontend tool this POST did not declare — Mastra still
holds the suspension, so falling through to RUN_FINISHED stranded it. The
parked lane's `finally` rescues that case via `suspensions.hasPending()`;
this lane has no live session to ask, so it raises instead.

commits.message: continue the run after a snapshot resume re-suspends
commits.body:
The crash-recovery resume lane (`resumeFromSnapshot`) answered a decision
card after a restart and then went silent: the run's events were only
RUN_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, RUN_FINISHED, and nothing was written to
thread history. Two gaps, both the same class as the three this lane has
already been patched for — things the parked lane gets from its live
Session that a re-assembled agent does not.

The lane runs under `approvalPolicy: "suspend"`, so the first thing a
recovered continuation usually does is park AGAIN on a gated tool. Mastra
reports that with a `tool-call-suspended` chunk and ends the stream — no

commits.message: rework report filters into searchable rows
commits.body:
The filter panel rendered five permanently-expanded checklists, each a
max-h-40 scroller over the full catalog. That does not survive hundreds
of projects, and it contradicted the data layer: an empty filter has
always meant "include everything", but the UI read as "curate a list"
and gave no signal that unchecked meant included.

Filters are now one row per dimension, always visible, defaulting to
"Alle". Values are picked in a searchable popover, never inline:

- Checkbox click toggles that item; label click solos it (select it,
  drop the rest). Solo is the common move at catalog scale, so it gets
  the larger hit area. The solo cues (underline + "nur") hang off their
  own hover zone so the checkbox never advertises them, and are
  hover-gated rather than data-selected because cmdk auto-selects the
  first item on open.
- Pattern filters (project name, client name, note) are evaluated
  server-side, so a saved report stays live as projects are added --
  an enumerated id list goes stale. project_name_contains also matches
  manual_project_title so manual entries are not silently dropped.
- Task filter gets a UI; task_ids already worked server-side.
- The phase filter no longer sits dead until a project is picked: with
  no project selected it loads phases across all projects.
- Grouping is capped at three dimensions, clamped on parse so a
  hand-edited URL or an older saved report cannot exceed it.

The sidebar toggle moves from the workspace topbar into the report
heading, per DocSidebarToggle's contract, and is renamed Einstellungen
-> Aufbau: this panel is not preferences beside the report, it is the
report's definition.

commits.message: refine the saved-reports UI
commits.body:
Follow-up polish on the reports sidebar, settings panel, grouped table and
print stylesheet.

Lint fixes so CI's changed-file check passes:

- Report deletion asks in-app via AlertDialog instead of window.confirm. The
  native dialog is unstyled, blocks the whole tab, and cannot be driven by
  tests. Mirrors the offers sidebar, and adds a `deleteConfirmDescription`
  string in both locales.
- The dimension drag handle states `role="button"` literally. dnd-kit's
  `attributes` spread already sets exactly that (its draggable default role IS
  "button"), but only a literal is visible to static a11y analysis, so the
  aria-label read as unsupported. It has to come after the spread — last wins —
  or TypeScript flags the duplicate.

Verified in the browser: the delete dialog renders with both locale strings,
Cancel closes it, and the saved report survives.

commits.message: rebuild the workspace when resuming from a snapshot
commits.body:
The parked lane reuses the original Session, which still carries the run's
Workspace and the sandbox instance attached to it. The snapshot lane assembles
a BRAND-NEW agent and passed it no workspace at all, so `ctx.workspace.sandbox`
was undefined for the continuation: after a server restart or a park TTL
expiry, resuming a suspended turn silently lost Code Mode and the workspace
file/skill tools, and the model reported them as unavailable mid-conversation.
Same class of gap the lane already fixed for frontend tools next to it.

The route now passes a `resolveWorkspace` thunk. It is lazy on purpose — the
parked fast path must never call it, or it would build a second sandbox
provider and run its syncIn over the staging dir the live one is using.

Nothing is parked on this lane, so the snapshot resume owns the sandbox
outright and tears it down in a `finally` — including the no-snapshot bail,
which is the easiest place to leak, since the workspace is already resolved by
the time we learn there is nothing to continue. A failed resolution is logged
and the resume continues: a degraded turn beats a stranded interrupt.

Rebuilding is safe because the container is keyed by lifecycle scope
(`engenty-session-<threadId>`), so a fresh instance reconnects to the same
container by label. Reusing a torn-down instance would not work at all —
Mastra latches status="destroyed" and ensureRunning() then throws
SandboxNotReadyError without reaching Docker.

Verified live: parked a run on a requestDecision card, restarted the AI
service to drop the park, answered the card. The resume took the snapshot lane
and built engenty-session-b309233c..., which was torn down when the run
finished. Both halves are mutation-checked by the new tests.

commits.message: create many tasks in one approved call
commits.body:
An agent building a project plan had no batched write: manage_project_task
created exactly one task per call, so a 40-task plan meant 40 gated calls,
40 round-trips and 40 approval prompts. Watching that loop is what surfaced
it — the model read the whole project tree, returned it as an 88 KB Code Mode
result, then started creating tasks one at a time.

projects_create_tasks takes up to 100 tasks and reads project settings ONCE
for the batch instead of per task, which is most of the per-call cost.

Deliberately NOT transactional: createTask fans out to the tasks module per
row, so there is no single statement to wrap. A bad row is reported in
`failed` and the rest of the batch still lands — a partial batch beats losing
39 good rows to one invalid status. Risk level, capabilities and the approval
gate match the singular op exactly, so one approval covering the batch is the
same authorization, not a weaker one.

The tool description tells the model to use create_many rather than looping
create, since the loop is what costs an approval per item.

commits.message: let Code Mode write behind the approval gate
commits.body:
Sandbox programs could only read. The wall was a SECOND fence in front of
core's authoritative gate, so removing it costs no authz: a write from a
sandbox program now needs a grant, exactly like a write from chat.

- engenty_tool_execute is exposed inside the sandbox with a `sandbox` option
  instead of `enforceReadOnly`. Reads run; a gated write without a grant
  returns `approval_required` and tells the model how to get one.
- New engenty_tools_preapprove: one card covers every write op a program
  will use, so a 200-row job asks once instead of 200 times. It drives the
  SAME gate cascade as execute — the interactive start lane gates under the
  "artifact" policy, not "suspend", which an earlier version got wrong.
- Delegated child runs inherit the parent's grants, so an approval given to
  the copilot is not re-asked by engenty.cli.

Approval cards: the artifact id is parsed the way the server encodes it
(first segment, decodeURIComponent) instead of being printed raw — a bulk
card used to show `%7B%22operation_ids%22...%7D`, and a secrets_reveal card
would have shown the secret's id. Bulk cards list every covered operation
and say "for this run"/"for this chat", since "once"/"always" promised the
wrong scope. Choice ids are unchanged; the resume route matches on them.

Suspend/park/resume durability:

- A parked run keeps its sandbox. Mastra's Sandbox._destroy() latches
  status="destroyed" (and returns early when the sandbox never started, so
  it does not even reach Docker), and the resume continues the SAME Session
  whose Workspace holds that instance — execute_typescript after an approval
  died with SandboxNotReadyError and no container ever existed. The park now
  owns the sandbox lifecycle like it owns the controller; teardown persists
  the workspace without destroying, and disposal happens on resume or TTL.
- requestDecision suspends natively instead of returning an artifact, so an
  answer resumes the run in place rather than re-running the turn.
- Suspended runs persist their transcript; `requires_action` runs used to
  write no thread_message rows, leaving history empty on every resume.
- Failed runs record why: an upstream provider failure (rate limit,
  content-policy block, timeout) left error_message NULL on the run row.

footers.value:
RUN_ERROR releases the composer instead of leaving it stuck on
"Stop generation"; the AG-UI inspector resets per thread (it reads a
server-wide firehose, so a new chat showed the previous thread's events)
and gained a Clear button. Tool-search results and Code Mode outcomes are
budget-capped to keep tool schemas from dominating the prompt.

Verified live at https://engenty.localhost: preapprove -> one card ->
"approve for this chat" -> one program created 3 time entries; and
requestDecision -> approve -> execute_typescript ran in the resumed run
with the sandbox container coming up and being torn down after.

commits.message:
perf(deploy): keep the dependency layer stable across releases

v0.1.108 moved `pnpm install` above the source copy so node_modules would stop
being rebuilt every release. It did not work, and v0.1.109 proved it: `RUN pnpm
install` executed (~614s for ai), prod re-pulled ~1 GB, and the deploy took 274s
— slightly worse than the 247s before the change.

The reason is that the deps stage does `COPY package.json ./`, and `pnpm
release` bumps `version` in that same root package.json on every single release.
The expensive layer was invalidated by the release process itself, forever. The
original verification missed this because it changed source files — never the
version — so it tested a scenario that does not occur.

Two fixes, because there were two instances of the same mistake:

1. A `manifests` stage normalises the version to 0.0.0-cache, and deps copies
   THAT. BuildKit keys `COPY --from` on the content of the copied path, so deps
   sees a byte-identical manifest across releases.

2. Each runtime stage copied root package.json ABOVE `COPY --from=deps
   /app/node_modules`. A changed layer forces every later layer in the stage to
   be rebuilt, and a rebuilt layer gets a fresh digest — so fix 1 alone would
   still have re-published the gigabyte. The volatile copies now come last.

The real version is restored in the runtime stage: prod is verified with
`docker exec ... head -3 /app/package.json`, which is what caught the three-day
stale-prod incident, and 0.0.0-cache would have silently broken it.

Verified against an actual release this time — two builds of the real
Dockerfile.ai in a throwaway worktree, bumping ONLY the version between them:

  #31 [deps 8/8] RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline  CACHED

12 of 16 layers shared. The 4 that differ are the two small ones per image
(971 kB manifests + 20.5 kB apps/ai/package.json). node_modules is byte
identical: ~1 GB of re-pull becomes ~1 MB. Both images report their true
version (0.1.109 / 0.1.110).

edge and app-host built and smoke-tested too rather than assumed from ai:
every runtime dep resolves from the app's own directory, ui/dist + manage ship,
edge boots to "Missing Supabase service configuration", and app-host's three
guards still pass (agentos patch, rivet-engine, agentos-sidecar).

This only helps releases that do not touch dependencies. A change to any
workspace package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, patches/ or scripts/ still rebuilds the
layer legitimately — v0.1.109 had exactly that (app-shell gained a dep), so it
would have re-pulled regardless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

perf(deploy): keep the dependency layer stable across releases

v0.1.108 moved `pnpm install` above the source copy so node_modules would stop
being rebuilt every release. It did not work, and v0.1.109 proved it: `RUN pnpm
install` executed (~614s for ai), prod re-pulled ~1 GB, and the deploy took 274s
— slightly worse than the 247s before the change.

The reason is that the deps stage does `COPY package.json ./`, and `pnpm
release` bumps `version` in that same root package.json on every single release.
The expensive layer was invalidated by the release process itself, forever. The
original verification missed this because it changed source files — never the
version — so it tested a scenario that does not occur.

Two fixes, because there were two instances of the same mistake:

1. A `manifests` stage normalises the version to 0.0.0-cache, and deps copies
   THAT. BuildKit keys `COPY --from` on the content of the copied path, so deps
   sees a byte-identical manifest across releases.

2. Each runtime stage copied root package.json ABOVE `COPY --from=deps
   /app/node_modules`. A changed layer forces every later layer in the stage to
   be rebuilt, and a rebuilt layer gets a fresh digest — so fix 1 alone would
   still have re-published the gigabyte. The volatile copies now come last.

The real version is restored in the runtime stage: prod is verified with
`docker exec ... head -3 /app/package.json`, which is what caught the three-day
stale-prod incident, and 0.0.0-cache would have silently broken it.

Verified against an actual release this time — two builds of the real
Dockerfile.ai in a throwaway worktree, bumping ONLY the version between them:

  #31 [deps 8/8] RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline  CACHED

12 of 16 layers shared. The 4 that differ are the two small ones per image
(971 kB manifests + 20.5 kB apps/ai/package.json). node_modules is byte
identical: ~1 GB of re-pull becomes ~1 MB. Both images report their true
version (0.1.109 / 0.1.110).

every runtime dep resolves from the app's own directory, ui/dist + manage ship,

commits.message:
perf(deploy): install dependencies before copying source

The deploy images copied the whole source tree above `pnpm install`, so every
commit rebuilt node_modules — and node_modules is the image. 3.7 GB
uncompressed, ~1 GB on the wire, against under 90 MB for everything that
actually changes in a release (packages 59 MB, modules 21 MB, dist 3 MB).

A rebuilt layer gets a new digest, so production re-downloaded that gigabyte on
every release even when the lockfile had not moved. Verified against the
registry: engenty-ai's largest layer is 602b784f… at v0.1.106 and 03492db8… at
v0.1.107, same 1076 MB, no dependency change between them. 03492db8 is one of
the layer ids visible in the deploy log.

That download is not merely slow, it is downtime. Coolify's compose build pack
has no rolling update: it removes the old containers and only then pulls. Of
v0.1.107's 239s outage, 188s was image pull and extract with the site already
dark.

So the deps stage now takes manifests only — lockfile, patches, the 85 workspace
package.json files, and scripts/ for the root postinstall hook. Source moves
down into the build stage. --parents keeps each manifest at its workspace path,
which needs the -labs frontend.

Verified rather than assumed, with an explicit local cache to take the builder's
GC out of it: build, change two source files, rebuild. Every step through
`pnpm install` was CACHED and the two images' layer sets came out identical —
nothing for production to re-pull.

@engenty/docs is excluded from the install because it is the one workspace with
an install hook (fumadocs-mdx), and that hook codegens from
apps/docs/source.config.ts — source this stage deliberately no longer has. The
first build failed there. Excluding the workspace is right for images that never
build docs; pulling its source back above the install would re-break the caching
this change exists to create.

.dockerignore now excludes nested node_modules too. A bare `node_modules`
pattern only matches the root one, so workspace node_modules were riding in with
the build context. Harmless while install ran after the source copy and
overwrote them; with this ordering they would land on top of the installed tree
and break pnpm's links. It also shrinks the context.

Both images were built and smoke-tested locally, not just compiled: every
runtime dependency resolves from the app's own directory (root node_modules
holds only the virtual store — resolving from /app is a false negative), and
each boots through its full import chain to the expected environment failure —
ai to the database-readiness gate, edge to "Missing Supabase service
configuration".

NOT a size win, contrary to what excluding a workspace suggests: the layer is
4.03 GB here against 3.7 GB in production. Slightly larger, cause unconfirmed.
The win is that it now stays identical across source-only releases.

The first release on this Dockerfile still pulls in full — its layer has no
ancestor to match. The payoff lands on the release after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(release): strip closed plugins when snapshot-publishing the mirror

The public repo's CI failed on every release:

  check-engenty-plugins: engenty.plugins lists 5 plugin(s) not on disk:
    - engenty-apps, engenty-remote, team-hr, time-tracking,
      team-chat-slack-bridge

The mirror is a filtered snapshot, so those modules are not in its tree — but
package.json still listed them, and plugins:check resolves every slug to an
on-disk plugin.

publish-open.sh has stripped them since the boundary existed. This script never
did, and this is the one CI runs (publish-open.yml calls
publish-open-snapshot.sh). Two publishers, one of them missing the step.

The transform has to be a pipe rather than the existing on-disk stripper:
this script builds its tree in a throwaway index and deliberately leaves the
working tree untouched, so package.json is rewritten in the index via
hash-object + update-index. Both share CLOSED_PLUGIN_SLUGS, so there is no new
list to drift. 2-space + trailing newline round-trips the repo's package.json
byte-for-byte, so the mirror sees the plugin removal and not a reformat.

Also adds a guard next to the existing excluded-paths one: refuse to publish
while a closed slug survives in engenty.plugins. A leak here does not expose
closed code, it red-lines the mirror's CI — which is exactly why this lasted, the
failure being on the other repo where nothing here was looking.

Verified with DRY_RUN=1 against the live public branch: one file changed,
1 insertion, 16 deletions — the five entries leaving package.json and nothing
else. Both guards pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
ci(deploy): fail the release when the deploy fails, not just when the trigger does

The deploy job queued a deployment and called that success. Everything that
actually breaks a deploy happens after that point, inside Coolify, where nothing
on GitHub was looking: an image it cannot pull, a migration that fails, a
container that never turns healthy.

That gap cost three days. v0.1.100 through v0.1.106 each reported a fully green
release while production sat on 0.1.99, because the ghcr credential on the VPS
had expired (GitHub's 30-day PAT default) and every deploy died in five seconds
at prepare_builder_image. Four consecutive failed deploys, zero red builds, and
no signal anywhere that prod had stopped moving.

So the job now waits for the outcome it was already responsible for:

- the trigger exports the deployment uuid — from the API body, or parsed out of
  the SSH forced command's "QUEUED uuid=..." line, so both routes stay
  verifiable rather than only the preferred one;
- a verify step polls GET /api/v1/deployments/{uuid} until terminal, failing the
  release on `failed`/`cancelled-by-user` and on a 15-minute timeout.

Being unable to verify is not the same as failing, so a missing uuid or absent
token warns instead of failing — but it says "NOT verified" rather than passing
silently, which was the whole defect.

No new credential: this reuses COOLIFY_API_TOKEN, already used to queue, over
443. Job timeout goes 5 -> 25 minutes because the job now waits (~4 min for a
cold pull plus migrations) instead of firing and forgetting.

Verified by replaying both extractions against real captured output: the API
body from run 31154656827 and the SSH line from the v0.1.106 recovery trigger.
Both scripts pass bash -n; the workflow parses.

Note this asserts Coolify finished the deploy, NOT that the running container
serves the released version. Closing that last gap needs a version endpoint on
edge — there is none today (/api/health 404s and openapi.json reports a
hardcoded 0.0.1).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.raw_message:
ci(deploy): fail the release when the deploy fails, not just when the trigger does

The deploy job queued a deployment and called that success. Everything that
actually breaks a deploy happens after that point, inside Coolify, where nothing
on GitHub was looking: an image it cannot pull, a migration that fails, a
container that never turns healthy.

That gap cost three days. v0.1.100 through v0.1.106 each reported a fully green
release while production sat on 0.1.99, because the ghcr credential on the VPS
had expired (GitHub's 30-day PAT default) and every deploy died in five seconds
at prepare_builder_image. Four consecutive failed deploys, zero red builds, and
no signal anywhere that prod had stopped moving.

So the job now waits for the outcome it was already responsible for:

- the trigger exports the deployment uuid — from the API body, or parsed out of
  the SSH forced command's "QUEUED uuid=..." line, so both routes stay
  verifiable rather than only the preferred one;
- a verify step polls GET /api/v1/deployments/{uuid} until terminal, failing the
  release on `failed`/`cancelled-by-user` and on a 15-minute timeout.

Being unable to verify is not the same as failing, so a missing uuid or absent
token warns instead of failing — but it says "NOT verified" rather than passing
silently, which was the whole defect.

No new credential: this reuses COOLIFY_API_TOKEN, already used to queue, over
443. Job timeout goes 5 -> 25 minutes because the job now waits (~4 min for a
cold pull plus migrations) instead of firing and forgetting.

Verified by replaying both extractions against real captured output: the API
body from run 31154656827 and the SSH line from the v0.1.106 recovery trigger.
Both scripts pass bash -n; the workflow parses.

Note this asserts Coolify finished the deploy, NOT that the running container
serves the released version. Closing that last gap needs a version endpoint on
edge — there is none today (/api/health 404s and openapi.json reports a
hardcoded 0.0.1).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): exit on SIGTERM instead of waiting to be killed

apps/ai had no way to stop. app.ts registers SIGTERM listeners to halt its
queue consumers, and registering ANY listener suppresses Node's default
terminate-on-SIGTERM — but nothing closed the HTTP server and nothing called
exit, so the listening socket kept the event loop alive until Docker gave up
and sent SIGKILL. Every stop cost the full kill timeout.

On a deploy that wait is pure downtime. Coolify removes the old containers
BEFORE starting the new stack (compose build packs get no rolling update: the
v0.1.106 log reads "Removing old containers." then, 63 seconds later, "Starting
new application", with image pulls accounting for 1 second of it), so the site
is already dark while we sit there being uninterruptible.

Shutdown is now ordered in index.ts: close the server, sweep sandboxes, exit —
under a hard deadline that must stay below the orchestrator's kill timeout, or
the graceful path is decorative.

The deadline is load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces, and the reason is
specific to this service. Two behaviours were measured on the pinned node:24
runtime rather than assumed:
  - close() alone drops idle keep-alive sockets by itself (Node >= 19), so an
    earlier closeIdleConnections() call was removed as dead weight;
  - close() will NOT interrupt an ACTIVE connection. A held-open SSE response
    left close() unresolved indefinitely (still hanging at 2.5s), while
    closeAllConnections() resolved it in 201ms. apps/ai streams agent runs over
    SSE, so without the deadline a single open stream would hold shutdown to
    SIGKILL and we would be exactly where we started.

The sandbox sweep becomes awaitable and loses its own signal handlers, since
shutdown is now ordered here. It only ever completed because nothing exited the
process: it was fire-and-forget, surviving on borrowed time until SIGKILL. A
prompt exit would have silently cut it off.

SCOPE: this is ai's contribution only, roughly the Docker default of 10s. It is
not all 63. edge and app-host register no SIGTERM listeners, so Node's default
already exits them promptly — ai was the only Node service hanging. What fills
the remaining ~50s is not yet identified; the next deploy's log will show it,
between those same two lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai-ui): report Auto effort in the control, not a toast

The Auto-resolved toast never dismissed and sat on top of the composer's
submit button, so a second message could not be sent without a reload.
Report the resolution in the effort control itself instead: the trigger
reads "Auto: <tier>" while highlighted, and the chooser marks the tier
Auto is currently running with a dot.

That mark needs a second lifetime — the flash is TTL'd, but "which tier
is Auto running" is a standing fact, so the store keeps a non-expiring
resolved slot beside the transient value. Highlight TTL 2.8s -> 8s now
that the control is the only surface reporting it.

Model ids follow the line the menu already draws for bound models and
appear in developer mode only. sonner drops out with the toast.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
chore(deps): upgrade @mastra/core 1.55.0 -> 1.57.0

Core-only bump: @mastra/pg 1.18.1, memory 1.24.0 and hono 1.5.12 all declare
peer ranges that already accept 1.57, so nothing else has to move.

1.57 carries fixes squarely in our HITL path: durable agents losing a pending
approval on page refresh, dropped tool results when toModelOutput returns
undefined, DurableAgent writing to a thread during suspension despite
memory.options.readOnly, and unbounded retention of suspended runs.

Re-authored the ChatChannelOutputProcessor patch — still not fixed upstream in
1.57, and dist chunk filenames rotate every release (agent-0y2cApTZ.js ->
agent-Dj30gJa3.js, plus the cjs twin). The hazard is unchanged: driverPromise
can reject before anything awaits it and take the process down.

Verified: apps/ai typecheck now 0 errors (the remaining Mastra-generics
failures are gone), apps/ai 816 tests and ai-ui 743 tests green, and a live
frontend-tool HITL cycle against the dev stack. That last one is where 1.57
shows: the scripted resume previously emitted only RUN_STARTED/RUN_FINISHED,
and now emits TOOL_CALL_RESULT plus the follow-up answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): merge thread metadata in the database, not across a stale read

updateThread read the thread row, folded active_artifact into the metadata
object in JS, then wrote the whole column back. Read and write are separate
transactions, so any metadata write committing in between was reverted — a
lost update wearing a merge's clothes. The old comment claimed the call
"never clobbers unrelated keys", which held only for keys present at read
time.

The window is not theoretical. Mastra rewrites this column itself (agent
state-signal tracking lives at metadata.mastra), the HITL lane writes
ag_ui_open_interrupt, and tool-approval grants write their own keys. Found
while gating PLAN-copilot-state-signals: a stale-read write reverted Mastra's
tracking v2 to v1, and because currentCacheKey then points at the old value,
the next matching update dedupes as "unchanged" and the agent silently keeps
stale state.

The new ai.merge_thread_metadata RPC applies a jsonb concat against the
CURRENT row in one statement, with deletion as p_remove_keys (a jsonb null
merges a null rather than dropping the key). INVOKER, matching the
owner-atomicity migration: this changes write atomicity, never write
authority — a non-owner still gets zero rows. An explicit `metadata` argument
keeps its full-replace semantics, because that is what the caller asked for.

Verified against the dev database: a concurrent metadata.mastra write and an
open interrupt both survive the artifact merge, clearing removes only its own
key, and a wrong owner is refused. The lost-update guard test is
mutation-checked — restoring the read-and-spread makes it fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
refactor(ai-ui): stop sending unread route scope on every run

forwardedProps.engenty.scope was built and shipped with every copilot run and
read on no code path. The only server reads of forwardedProps.engenty are
effort (thread-run-routes.ts:255) and model_id (:317) — no dynamic key access
and no spread anywhere, so nothing consumed it.

The agent's route facts already arrive by two other channels: the
AgentUiStateSnapshot in `state`, which the prompt header declares authoritative
for route and selection, and the four `context` entries. scope was a third
copy that reached no reader.

Found while scoping PLAN-copilot-state-signals, which replaces the per-turn
route blob with a Mastra state signal; this part needed no replacement because
nothing was using it.

The test that pinned the old behaviour now pins its absence — an unread key on
every run is pure wire weight and should not drift back in unnoticed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): stop rebuilding thread metadata from stale reads across the HITL lane

Sweep of the pattern fixed for active_artifact in 71842afeb. Nine more sites
merged a key onto a previously-read metadata object and wrote the whole column,
so any key written in between was reverted.

The run-lane ones had the longest window by far: `let hsSessionMetadata =
session.metadata` is captured when the HTTP request arrives and written back
when the turn suspends — seconds to minutes later. That made this a live bug,
not a latent one: an agent that calls show_artifact mid-turn and then suspends
for approval had active_artifact reverted by its own interrupt write, silently
undoing the multi-window sync 9c538e59b shipped. The existing workaround
(threading the metadata object forward so a grant "would not be erased") was
the same problem seen from the inside.

Grants needed more than the 5-arg merge: they are arrays appended to, so a
patch built from a stale read replaces the whole list and drops a concurrent
grant — the same lost update one level down. merge_thread_metadata gains
p_append_sets, a set-union evaluated against the current row, and the old
signature is dropped rather than overloaded.

Converted: emit-interrupt (3), thread-run-routes (4), resume-conversation-run,
reconcile-orphaned-interrupt, realtime-tool-routes, function-provider. Local
copies stay where they feed this request's in-process gate re-check; only the
database write changed. The one remaining whole-column write is the explicit
`metadata` argument on updateThread, which is a deliberate full replace.

Verified live against the dev stack: suspend a frontend-tool turn, inject
active_artifact and a metadata.mastra state-signal entry while it is parked,
then resume — the interrupt clears and both injected keys survive. Both were
reverted before. apps/ai typecheck clean, 819 tests green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(ai): publish window route state as a Mastra state signal (server half)

PLAN-copilot-state-signals Phase B, server side. POST
/ai/v1/threads/:threadId/state takes an AgentUiStateSnapshotV1 plus a window id
and forwards it to agent.sendStateSignal as a per-window lane. No client calls
it yet — B1/B4 follow.

Deliberately not a run. ifIdle is "persist", so a navigation reaches the thread
without starting or billing a turn; ifActive is "deliver" so navigating
mid-stream joins the run in flight. That one option is the whole safety story of
the feature — "wake" would bill a turn per navigation — so it is pinned by a
test, and the carrier agent is built with a model that throws if anything ever
reaches it.

One lane per window (route:<windowId>). A signal lane is thread-scoped while
route context is per-window, so a single lane would let a background window
redefine what the agent thinks the user is looking at. The cache key is built
from the semantic fields only: observed_at, sequence and snapshot_id are
refreshed on every recompute and would defeat dedupe entirely.

An invalid or oversized snapshot is rejected loudly here, unlike the run route,
which drops one silently and proceeds with no snapshot at all — the agent then
flies blind with no trace.

Verified live against the dev stack: first publish persists, republishing the
same route returns skipped/unchanged, navigating persists again, a second
window opens its own lane, a malformed snapshot 400s, and the thread stays
idle throughout. Lanes land in ai.thread.metadata.mastra.stateSignals through
our own memory storage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): stop discarding Mastra message metadata

ai.thread_message had no metadata column, and the storage mapped messages in as
{role, parts, author_user_id} only. Everything Mastra hangs off
content.metadata was therefore dropped on write — not just for one feature.

Found via state signals, which keep their identity there
(metadata.signal = {id, type:"state", ...}). Without it getActiveStateSignals
cannot reconstruct a signal when the thread is loaded, so signals persisted as
inert system text.

Adds the column (jsonb, default '{}'), carries content.metadata through
appendMessage, and merges it back under the projected author_user_id on read.
author_user_id stays a column projection and is deliberately not written into
the blob, so it cannot drift between the two.

The row type keeps metadata optional: rows are also synthesized in memory
(snapshot healing, placeholder assistant rows) where there is nothing to carry.

Verified on the dev database: a state signal now round-trips with
{"signal":{"type":"state","metadata":{"state":{"id":"route:win-a",...}}}}
intact, where it was previously absent.

NOTE: necessary but not sufficient for state signals to reach the model. A live
probe on a thread holding three signals still answers that "win-b" does not
appear in its context, so the consumption path needs its own investigation —
see PLAN-copilot-state-signals Phase C.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): preserve Mastra's "signal" message role

The storage coerced role "signal" into "system" because the
ai.session_message_role enum had no such value. Mastra rebuilds state signals
with a hard filter — dbMessagesToStateSignals keeps only
`message.role === "signal"` — so every coerced row was invisible to it and the
agent could not see the state at all.

Adds "signal" to the enum, stops the coercion, and excludes the role from the
transcript builder: signals are agent-facing state, not conversation turns, and
must never surface as chat bubbles. The exclusion is a flatMap rather than a
filter so the narrowing is the type system's job, not a cast.

The test that pinned the old behaviour ("keeps a non-user signal as a system
message") pinned the bug; it now pins the role and metadata surviving the write.

Verified on the dev database: state signals persist as role=signal carrying
{"signal":{"type":"state","metadata":{"state":{"id":"route:win-a",
"threadId":"<matching>"}}}} — which is exactly the shape Mastra's filter wants.

resolveStateSignalHistory is only reachable from a processor path

into the prompt on its own — consuming them requires an input processor with a
stateId implementing computeStateSignal. A live probe on a thread holding three
correctly-shaped signals still answers that "win-b" is absent from its context.
That processor is what Phase C actually is; it is not a prompt-rendering tweak.

This reverts commit d0ad65a13.

own. Consuming them means writing an input processor that renders state into
the prompt — which is the job formatAgentUiStateHarnessInstructions already
does today, with four migrations of setup around it and nothing deleted in
exchange.

So this removes a POST /ai/v1/threads/:threadId/state that no client calls. An
unreachable write endpoint on the AI service is a surface to defend, not a
head start, and a dead code path rots faster than it would cost to retype.

only found through this work:

Mastra store, whether or not we ever send a state signal.

Still worth revisiting if Mastra starts injecting state signals natively, or
for a coordinator that must observe a user's navigation between turns — the one
property our per-run instruction block genuinely cannot provide.

commits.message: publish window route state as a Mastra state signal (server half)
commits.body:
PLAN-copilot-state-signals Phase B, server side. POST
/ai/v1/threads/:threadId/state takes an AgentUiStateSnapshotV1 plus a window id
and forwards it to agent.sendStateSignal as a per-window lane. No client calls
it yet — B1/B4 follow.

Deliberately not a run. ifIdle is "persist", so a navigation reaches the thread
without starting or billing a turn; ifActive is "deliver" so navigating
mid-stream joins the run in flight. That one option is the whole safety story of
the feature — "wake" would bill a turn per navigation — so it is pinned by a
test, and the carrier agent is built with a model that throws if anything ever
reaches it.

One lane per window (route:<windowId>). A signal lane is thread-scoped while
route context is per-window, so a single lane would let a background window
redefine what the agent thinks the user is looking at. The cache key is built
from the semantic fields only: observed_at, sequence and snapshot_id are
refreshed on every recompute and would defeat dedupe entirely.

An invalid or oversized snapshot is rejected loudly here, unlike the run route,
which drops one silently and proceeds with no snapshot at all — the agent then
flies blind with no trace.

Verified live against the dev stack: first publish persists, republishing the
same route returns skipped/unchanged, navigating persists again, a second
window opens its own lane, a malformed snapshot 400s, and the thread stays
idle throughout. Lanes land in ai.thread.metadata.mastra.stateSignals through
our own memory storage.

commits.message: stop rebuilding thread metadata from stale reads across the HITL lane
commits.body:
Sweep of the pattern fixed for active_artifact in 71842afeb. Nine more sites
merged a key onto a previously-read metadata object and wrote the whole column,
so any key written in between was reverted.

The run-lane ones had the longest window by far: `let hsSessionMetadata =
session.metadata` is captured when the HTTP request arrives and written back
when the turn suspends — seconds to minutes later. That made this a live bug,
not a latent one: an agent that calls show_artifact mid-turn and then suspends
for approval had active_artifact reverted by its own interrupt write, silently
undoing the multi-window sync 9c538e59b shipped. The existing workaround
(threading the metadata object forward so a grant "would not be erased") was
the same problem seen from the inside.

Grants needed more than the 5-arg merge: they are arrays appended to, so a
patch built from a stale read replaces the whole list and drops a concurrent
grant — the same lost update one level down. merge_thread_metadata gains
p_append_sets, a set-union evaluated against the current row, and the old
signature is dropped rather than overloaded.

footers.value:
emit-interrupt (3), thread-run-routes (4), resume-conversation-run,
reconcile-orphaned-interrupt, realtime-tool-routes, function-provider. Local
copies stay where they feed this request's in-process gate re-check; only the
database write changed. The one remaining whole-column write is the explicit
`metadata` argument on updateThread, which is a deliberate full replace.

Verified live against the dev stack: suspend a frontend-tool turn, inject
active_artifact and a metadata.mastra state-signal entry while it is parked,
then resume — the interrupt clears and both injected keys survive. Both were
reverted before. apps/ai typecheck clean, 819 tests green.

commits.message: merge thread metadata in the database, not across a stale read
commits.body:
updateThread read the thread row, folded active_artifact into the metadata
object in JS, then wrote the whole column back. Read and write are separate
transactions, so any metadata write committing in between was reverted — a
lost update wearing a merge's clothes. The old comment claimed the call
"never clobbers unrelated keys", which held only for keys present at read
time.

The window is not theoretical. Mastra rewrites this column itself (agent
state-signal tracking lives at metadata.mastra), the HITL lane writes
ag_ui_open_interrupt, and tool-approval grants write their own keys. Found
while gating PLAN-copilot-state-signals: a stale-read write reverted Mastra's
tracking v2 to v1, and because currentCacheKey then points at the old value,
the next matching update dedupes as "unchanged" and the agent silently keeps
stale state.

The new ai.merge_thread_metadata RPC applies a jsonb concat against the
CURRENT row in one statement, with deletion as p_remove_keys (a jsonb null
merges a null rather than dropping the key). INVOKER, matching the
owner-atomicity migration: this changes write atomicity, never write
authority — a non-owner still gets zero rows. An explicit `metadata` argument
keeps its full-replace semantics, because that is what the caller asked for.

Verified against the dev database: a concurrent metadata.mastra write and an
open interrupt both survive the artifact merge, clearing removes only its own
key, and a wrong owner is refused. The lost-update guard test is
mutation-checked — restoring the read-and-spread makes it fail.

commits.message: report Auto effort in the control, not a toast
commits.body:
The Auto-resolved toast never dismissed and sat on top of the composer's
submit button, so a second message could not be sent without a reload.
Report the resolution in the effort control itself instead: the trigger
reads "Auto: <tier>" while highlighted, and the chooser marks the tier
Auto is currently running with a dot.

commits.message:
refactor(ai)!: rename thread/session DAL, routes, and service layer

TRK-08: the DB was renamed agent_session -> thread and agent_session_run
-> agent_run, but the TypeScript layer never followed. This lands three
of the sized slices from the infra audit's consolidation path:

- DAL (apps/ai/src/dal/agent-sessions/ -> dal/threads/): ThreadRow,
  ThreadMessageRow, AgentRunRow, ThreadStore, createThreadStore with
  Thread-named methods (getThread, upsertThread, listThreadsForUser,
  etc.) and matching return shapes.
- Routes (agent-sessions-routes.ts / agent-session-runs-routes.ts ->
  thread-routes.ts / thread-run-routes.ts): registerThreadRoutes,
  registerThreadRunRoutes, onThreadPersisted/onThreadDeleted callbacks.
  URL paths already said /threads; only the code names catch up.
- Service (session-service.ts): createThreadService/ThreadService,
  AiService.sessions -> AiService.threads, and the six thread-CRUD
  methods (listThreads, createThread, getThread, updateThread,
  deleteThread(s)).

Deliberately NOT renamed — different concepts, not the Thread entity:
AiSessionScope/AiScopeCredential (the caller's auth scope), the live
in-memory ConversationSession in session-park.ts (still non-durable,
tracked separately), CascadeSessionScope (a voice-call session), and
AiSessionError/AiSessionErrorCode (already emits correct agent_threads.*
codes; renaming the wrapper class is a smaller follow-up).

Wire contracts preserved: JSON response bodies still key off `session`/
`sessions` (packages/ai-ui and modules/engenty-copilot parse these) —
only the internal service-layer variable names changed, remapped at
each response boundary.

Typecheck steady at the pre-existing apps/ai baseline (174 errors, all
predating this change, confirmed via diff). Full suite: 127 files /
741 tests green.

Remaining from the TRK-08 map: modules/engenty-copilot server + UI and
packages/ai-ui's stragglers (frontend side of this same facade).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(ai): durable chat run tracking, fail-loud choice resolution, cross-window sync

Chat runs executed durably but invisibly: the conversation lane never wrote
ai.agent_run / ai.agent_run_event (the session run tracker was wired into the
headless, delegate, and action lanes only). A reloaded client listing session
runs found nothing to reattach to, and a second window on the same thread had
nothing to discover — messages sent before a reload looked lost even though
the run completed and persisted server-side.

- Wire createSessionRunTracker into startConversationRun and
  resumeConversationRun: the tracker publishes to the in-process bus with the
  same seq it persists, so reload/other windows list the run and replay
  ?since=. Run rows are closed in finally (waiting -> requires_action,
  failed -> failed, aborted -> cancelled, else completed) with token usage.
- Client recovery hook: when a realtime signal lands and no run is live, apply
  the persisted transcript whenever it is ahead of the in-memory lane (a
  SUCCEEDED run previously applied nothing — only cancelled/failed unflushed
  text was handled), and sync the open-interrupt chip from thread metadata so
  a decision answered in another window clears everywhere.
- Decision resumes no longer silently deny on an id-only payload:
  resolveDecisionResumeChoice matches choice_id against the interrupt's own
  choices (label recovered when known); an unknown id is rejected with
  400 agent_threads.unresolvedChoice instead of being read as "not approved".

Verified live: kill connection mid-stream -> fresh client finds the running
run and replays RUN_STARTED -> full text -> RUN_FINISHED; decision interrupts
land requires_action; 771 apps/ai + 695 ai-ui tests green.

commits.message:
feat(ai): parallel live streaming into attached chat windows

A second window (or a reloaded one) attaching to an in-flight run previously
showed nothing until the run finished: the attach filter dropped ALL
TEXT_MESSAGE_* events (the "DB snapshot owns text" rule), and the user turn
existed nowhere the attacher could see it before the end-of-turn flush.

- Server: emit a CUSTOM engenty.user_message event (client message id + text)
  right after RUN_STARTED, so attachers can render the user bubble live.
- Client: replace the blanket text drop with a per-message replay filter —
  messages the DB snapshot already carries stay snapshot-owned (no partial-
  flush doubling), messages the snapshot has never seen stream live, which is
  every in-flight chat turn. The user bubble is synthesized from the CUSTOM
  event with id-dedupe against the lane.

Verified live: second client attached mid-run received the user_message event
at +0.01s and 53 text deltas concurrently with the originating window's
stream; both received RUN_FINISHED in the same instant. 13 route + 697 ai-ui
tests green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
fix(ai): persist post-resume text, stop attach self-duplication in chat sync

Two defects found live-testing multi-window chat sync:

1. Reload lost the final answer of any HITL turn. A turn that suspends
   mid-message (frontend tool / artifact show) flushes the PARTIAL assistant
   row at suspend time; at resume-finish Mastra re-saves the same message id
   with the full part list — and appendMessage's ignoreDuplicates upsert
   silently dropped it. saveMessages now routes re-saves of existing
   assistant/tool messages through updateMessageParts (no-op when parts are
   unchanged); user re-saves stay insert-once so folded attachment parts
   survive.

2. The sending window duplicated its own final message up to 4x. The artifact
   auto-resume dispatch leaves submitInFlight false, so the window's realtime
   'running' signal attached it to the run its own POST was already streaming
   — and at run end, three signals raced through resumeActiveRun before the
   loop's async 'running' flag was set, each replaying the full event log.
   Three guards: skip attaching to the locally-streamed run (client resume
   reuses the client-supplied runId), a synchronous dispatch latch, and the
   replay filter now refuses text for any message id the lane already renders.

Also: recoveryAttemptedRef is set BEFORE launching from the realtime path
(the loop's own submitStatus flip re-ran the mount effect, which aborted the
attach it was reacting to — second window never streamed), the mount effect
no longer aborts a streaming loop on dep changes, and the thread-watch
realtime channel subscribes once per (client, thread) instead of resubscribing
every render — signals landing in the resubscribe gaps were lost.

Verified in-browser: artifact flow renders once in the sending window
(recovery log shows only 'skipped: locally streamed run'), persisted parts
carry the trailing text, second-window live streaming intact. 698 + 774
tests green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
refactor(ai): user-turn echo as protocol-native role:user text messages

The CUSTOM engenty.user_message event reinvented something AG-UI already
specifies: TEXT_MESSAGE_START carries a role union that includes "user".
The run stream now echoes the user turn as a standard role:"user" text trio,
and the custom event + its client-side synthesis are deleted.

- conversation reducer: upsertStreamedMessage honors the START event's role
  (unknown/missing roles stay assistant; tool-call paths unchanged). User
  messages are write-once in the lane — the SENDING window holds the
  optimistic user message under the same id, and the echo's delta must not
  double its text (the echo also flows through the sender's own POST stream).
- attached-window replay needs no special case anymore: the trio passes the
  same per-message gating as assistant text (admitted when neither snapshot
  nor lane has the id) and the lane renders the user bubble natively.

Verified live: second window renders the user bubble + streamed reply from
the native events, event log seq 1-3 = TEXT_MESSAGE_START(role user)/CONTENT/
END, no duplication in the sending window. 701 + 774 tests green.

commits.message:
fix(ai): attached windows lose the user turn — close the attach seam, unify user message id

Two stacked defects made a second window consistently render an empty user
bubble (and never heal after the run finished):

1. Attach seam: the run stream routes subscribed to the live bus and then
   replayed persisted rows — an event published before the subscribe but
   committed after the read arrived through neither source. Persistence lags
   publish (unawaited inserts + delta coalescing), and the user-turn trio is
   emitted exactly in that window. run-event-bus now keeps a full in-memory
   event buffer per live run; both attach routes read it in the same tick as
   the subscribe, so live runs are served seamlessly from memory (DB replay
   remains for non-live runs, and for the capped-buffer prefix).

2. Id split: the durable user row was persisted under a Mastra-generated id
   while the stream trio uses the client-assigned id, so lanes and snapshots
   could neither dedupe nor heal the same message. The session memory storage
   now adopts the client userMessageId for the current turn's new user insert
   (history rows and re-saves stay insert-once).

Live-proven with two browser tabs on one thread: the passive tab renders the
user bubble with text mid-stream, single copies in both tabs, and the DB row
id now equals the streamed trio id.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
feat(ai): make show_artifact state-backed so the presented artifact syncs across windows

Frontend tools execute in exactly one window (they resume the run), so their
EFFECTS could not reach other windows attached to the same thread. Rather
than mirroring tool execution, move show_artifact's effect into shared
state — the same shape that already makes theme changes sync for free:

- New ai.thread metadata key `active_artifact` ({artifact_id, shown_at}),
  with merge/read helpers in @engenty/ag-ui-bridge that touch only that key.
- Thread PATCH accepts active_artifact_id; the service merges it onto the
  CURRENT row so HITL interrupt/grant keys are never clobbered.
- The show_artifact handler keeps its instant local activate, then persists
  the id best-effort.
- Every other window picks it up on the ai.thread realtime channel it is
  already subscribed to and applies the same policy as a freshly-created
  artifact: auto-focus if its pane is open, otherwise badge it. paneOpen /
  paneExpanded stay per-window — sharing those would let one window close
  another's pane.

Also: Mastra's saveThread full-replaces the metadata column from a
load-time snapshot, so an active_artifact write landing between two Mastra
saves was silently wiped (observed live: metadata back to {}). Added the key
to the externally-owned set that saveThread re-injects from the DB row, and
renamed that set from HITL_* since it now covers more than HITL.

Verified live with two tabs on one thread: passive tab did not steal focus,
its topbar read "Artefakt-Panel öffnen (1 neu)", and opening it landed on
the exact artifact the agent presented. 787 apps/ai + 703 ai-ui + 36
ag-ui-bridge tests green.

commits.message:
fix(ai-ui): attached windows stop duplicating the current turn; artifact card + pane survive reload/sync

Three live-testing defects from the D7 multi-window work, all client-side:

1) Duplicated streaming in attached windows. Mastra's session stream ids and
   its persisted MessageList ids are independently generated (structural in
   1.55 — createEmptyAssistantMessage rotates a fresh generateId per step, and
   the resume re-save matches rows by the Mastra id, so server-side adoption
   like the user-id fix would break suspend/resume updateMessageParts). Mastra
   also flushes the partial assistant row after EVERY tool call, so a mid-turn
   attach saw the turn twice under two ids that no dedupe could match:
   - partitionSnapshotForRunAttach: rows persisted BY the attached run
     (created_at >= run start) are replay-owned — dropped from the attach
     snapshot and purged from a reload-hydrated lane; the replay re-streams
     them. Rows older than the run (a resume's pre-suspend flush — resume is a
     NEW run, seq restarts at 0, never re-delivers) are kept.
   - shouldApplyTerminalRunMessagesSnapshot: the count-based gate was blind to
     the id split (a lane holding BOTH copies is LONGER than truth, heal
     rejected forever). Text compare on the last assistant instead; used by
     the terminal re-sync and a new post-attach authoritative re-sync so every
     attached run ends on DB identity (and the coalescer's final flush racing
     RUN_FINISHED just defers the heal instead of losing text).

2) Empty artifact pane in the passive window: the active-artifact signal could
   outrun the tenant-wide ai.artifact invalidation, activating a tab the stale
   list didn't carry. The pane handler now invalidates artifactsQueryRoot on
   the same signal.

3) Artifact card folded into "Used N tools" after reload: live streaming
   splits a turn across rotated assistant messages (tools after that
   message's last text -> inline card), but the persisted row coalesces the
   turn into ONE message (tools before the last text -> collapsed timeline).
   New `standalone` flag on ToolCallUiRegistration + hasStandaloneToolCallUi
   in the transcript escape list; set on the artifact and generative-UI cards.

Live-verified by Matthias with two windows (no duplication during/after the
turn, pane syncs with content, card survives reload). 183 copilot + 150
apps-ai/artifacts + 23 gating tests green; recovery-test fixtures moved run
start after the fixture rows to keep exercising the pre-run hydration path,
plus a new purge regression test.

commits.message: make show_artifact state-backed so the presented artifact syncs across windows
commits.body:
Frontend tools execute in exactly one window (they resume the run), so their
EFFECTS could not reach other windows attached to the same thread. Rather
than mirroring tool execution, move show_artifact's effect into shared
state — the same shape that already makes theme changes sync for free:

- New ai.thread metadata key `active_artifact` ({artifact_id, shown_at}),
  with merge/read helpers in @engenty/ag-ui-bridge that touch only that key.
- Thread PATCH accepts active_artifact_id; the service merges it onto the
  CURRENT row so HITL interrupt/grant keys are never clobbered.
- The show_artifact handler keeps its instant local activate, then persists
  the id best-effort.
- Every other window picks it up on the ai.thread realtime channel it is
  already subscribed to and applies the same policy as a freshly-created
  artifact: auto-focus if its pane is open, otherwise badge it. paneOpen /
  paneExpanded stay per-window — sharing those would let one window close
  another's pane.

footers.value:
Mastra's saveThread full-replaces the metadata column from a
load-time snapshot, so an active_artifact write landing between two Mastra
saves was silently wiped (observed live: metadata back to {}). Added the key
to the externally-owned set that saveThread re-injects from the DB row, and
renamed that set from HITL_* since it now covers more than HITL.

Verified live with two tabs on one thread: passive tab did not steal focus,
its topbar read "Artefakt-Panel öffnen (1 neu)", and opening it landed on
the exact artifact the agent presented. 787 apps/ai + 703 ai-ui + 36
ag-ui-bridge tests green.

commits.message: attached windows lose the user turn — close the attach seam, unify user message id
commits.body:
Two stacked defects made a second window consistently render an empty user
bubble (and never heal after the run finished):

1. Attach seam: the run stream routes subscribed to the live bus and then
   replayed persisted rows — an event published before the subscribe but
   committed after the read arrived through neither source. Persistence lags
   publish (unawaited inserts + delta coalescing), and the user-turn trio is
   emitted exactly in that window. run-event-bus now keeps a full in-memory
   event buffer per live run; both attach routes read it in the same tick as
   the subscribe, so live runs are served seamlessly from memory (DB replay
   remains for non-live runs, and for the capped-buffer prefix).

2. Id split: the durable user row was persisted under a Mastra-generated id
   while the stream trio uses the client-assigned id, so lanes and snapshots
   could neither dedupe nor heal the same message. The session memory storage
   now adopts the client userMessageId for the current turn's new user insert
   (history rows and re-saves stay insert-once).

Live-proven with two browser tabs on one thread: the passive tab renders the
user bubble with text mid-stream, single copies in both tabs, and the DB row
id now equals the streamed trio id.

commits.message: user-turn echo as protocol-native role:user text messages
commits.body:
The CUSTOM engenty.user_message event reinvented something AG-UI already
specifies: TEXT_MESSAGE_START carries a role union that includes "user".
The run stream now echoes the user turn as a standard role:"user" text trio,
and the custom event + its client-side synthesis are deleted.

- conversation reducer: upsertStreamedMessage honors the START event's role
  (unknown/missing roles stay assistant; tool-call paths unchanged). User
  messages are write-once in the lane — the SENDING window holds the
  optimistic user message under the same id, and the echo's delta must not
  double its text (the echo also flows through the sender's own POST stream).
- attached-window replay needs no special case anymore: the trio passes the
  same per-message gating as assistant text (admitted when neither snapshot
  nor lane has the id) and the lane renders the user bubble natively.

Verified live: second window renders the user bubble + streamed reply from
the native events, event log seq 1-3 = TEXT_MESSAGE_START(role user)/CONTENT/
END, no duplication in the sending window. 701 + 774 tests green.

commits.message: persist post-resume text, stop attach self-duplication in chat sync
commits.body:
Two defects found live-testing multi-window chat sync:

1. Reload lost the final answer of any HITL turn. A turn that suspends
   mid-message (frontend tool / artifact show) flushes the PARTIAL assistant
   row at suspend time; at resume-finish Mastra re-saves the same message id
   with the full part list — and appendMessage's ignoreDuplicates upsert
   silently dropped it. saveMessages now routes re-saves of existing
   assistant/tool messages through updateMessageParts (no-op when parts are
   unchanged); user re-saves stay insert-once so folded attachment parts
   survive.

2. The sending window duplicated its own final message up to 4x. The artifact
   auto-resume dispatch leaves submitInFlight false, so the window's realtime
   'running' signal attached it to the run its own POST was already streaming
   — and at run end, three signals raced through resumeActiveRun before the
   loop's async 'running' flag was set, each replaying the full event log.
   Three guards: skip attaching to the locally-streamed run (client resume
   reuses the client-supplied runId), a synchronous dispatch latch, and the
   replay filter now refuses text for any message id the lane already renders.

footers.value:
recoveryAttemptedRef is set BEFORE launching from the realtime path
(the loop's own submitStatus flip re-ran the mount effect, which aborted the
attach it was reacting to — second window never streamed), the mount effect
no longer aborts a streaming loop on dep changes, and the thread-watch
realtime channel subscribes once per (client, thread) instead of resubscribing
every render — signals landing in the resubscribe gaps were lost.

Verified in-browser: artifact flow renders once in the sending window
(recovery log shows only 'skipped: locally streamed run'), persisted parts
carry the trailing text, second-window live streaming intact. 698 + 774
tests green.
